title.zh: 卷四十二 列傳第三十: 王肅 劉芳 常爽
title.en: Volume 42 Biographies 30: Wang Su, Liu Fang, Chang Shuang
title.raw: 卷四十二 列傳第三十: 王肅 劉芳 常爽 Volume 42 Biographies 30: Wang Su, Liu Fang, Chang Shuang

sentences.zh: 王肅 劉芳 常爽

translations.literal: Wang Su, Liu Fang, Chang Shuang
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, Liu Fang, and Chang Shuang

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Thirty
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 30

sentences.zh: 王肅劉芳孫逖芳從子懋常爽孫景

translations.literal: Wang Su; Liu Fang's grandson Ti; Fang's nephew Mao; Chang Shuang's grandson Jing
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su; Liu Fang's grandson Ti; Fang's nephew Mao; and Chang Shuang's grandson Jing

sentences.zh: 王肅，字恭懿，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Su, styled Gongyi, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, whose courtesy name was Gongyi, came from Linyi in Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 父奐，齊雍州刺史，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Huan was Qi Governor of Yong Province; the Southern History has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan had served as governor of Yong Province under Qi; his biography appears in the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 肅少聰辯，涉獵經史，頗有大志。

translations.literal: Su in youth was clever and eloquent, ranged through the classics and histories, and had rather great ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Su was quick-witted and articulate; he read widely in the classics and histories and harbored considerable ambition.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位秘書丞。

translations.literal: He served Qi and held the post of Secretaryship Aide.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Qi service and rose to the post of secretaryship aide.

sentences.zh: 父奐及兄弟並為齊武帝所殺。

translations.literal: His father Huan and his brothers were all killed by Emperor Wu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan and his brothers were all put to death by Emperor Wu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，肅自建鄴來奔。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, Su came from Jiankang to defect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Taihe reign (493), Su fled from Jiankang and came over to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 孝文幸鄴，聞其至，虛衿待之，引見問故。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was visiting Ye; hearing of his arrival, he opened his bosom to receive him, summoned him for audience, and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen happened to be at Ye; when he heard of Su's arrival he received him with open arms, summoned him for an audience, and asked why he had come.

sentences.zh: 肅辭義敏切，辯而有禮，帝甚哀惻之。

translations.literal: Su's words were keen and to the point, argumentative yet with propriety; the emperor greatly pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Su spoke with sharp clarity and courteous force; the emperor was deeply moved with pity for him.

sentences.zh: 遂語及為國之道。

translations.literal: They then spoke of the way to govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: The conversation soon turned to the principles of governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 肅所陳說，深會旨，帝促席移景，不覺坐之疲也。

translations.literal: What Su set forth deeply hit the mark; the emperor drew his mat closer and the sun moved on its course without his noticing weariness from sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Everything Su proposed struck the emperor to the heart; Xiaowen drew his seat nearer as the hours passed and never noticed how long he had been sitting.

sentences.zh: 肅因言蕭氏危亡之兆，可以乘機，帝於是圖南之規轉銳。

translations.literal: Su thereupon spoke of signs that the Xiao house was near peril and ruin, that opportunity might be seized; the emperor's plan to march south then grew keener.
translations.idiomatic: Su went on to describe the signs that the house of Xiao was heading toward collapse and argued that the moment could be seized; from then on the emperor's designs on the south sharpened markedly.

sentences.zh: 器重禮遇，日有加焉；

translations.literal: Esteem and courteous treatment increased day by day;
translations.idiomatic: The esteem and honors shown him grew day by day;

sentences.zh: 親貴舊臣莫之間也，或屏左右，談說至夜分不罷。

translations.literal: none among the intimate nobles and old ministers could come between them; sometimes they dismissed attendants and talked on until deep night without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: and none of the emperor's closest kin or veteran ministers could come between them. Sometimes they dismissed their attendants and talked on deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 肅亦盡忠輸誠，無所隱避，自謂君臣之際，猶孔明之遇玄德也。

translations.literal: Su also gave his utmost loyalty and poured out sincerity without concealment, deeming the relation between lord and minister like Kongming's meeting with Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Su for his part gave his full loyalty and held nothing back, comparing the bond between himself and his sovereign to Zhuge Liang's meeting with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 尋除輔國、大將軍長史，賜爵開陽伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief Clerk to the General Who Assists the State and the Grand General, and enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made chief clerk to the General Who Assists the State and the grand general, and enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiyang.

sentences.zh: 肅固辭伯爵，許之。

translations.literal: Su firmly declined the baron's rank and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Su firmly declined the baron's title, and the emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 詔肅討齊義陽，聽招募壯勇以為爪牙，其募士有功，賞加等。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Su to campaign against Qi's Yiyang; he was permitted to recruit stalwart braves as claws and teeth, and for recruited soldiers with merit rewards were raised a grade.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Su to campaign against Yiyang in Qi territory and authorized him to recruit bold fighters as his shock troops; recruits who distinguished themselves were to receive rewards one grade higher than usual.

sentences.zh: 其從肅行者，六品已下聽先擬用，以後聞；

translations.literal: Those who followed Su on campaign, of sixth rank and below, were permitted provisional appointment first, with report afterward;
translations.idiomatic: Men of sixth rank and below who accompanied him might be provisionally appointed on his recommendation, with formal notification to follow;

sentences.zh: 若投化人，聽五品已下先即優授。

translations.literal: if defectors, those of fifth rank and below might at once receive preferential appointment.
translations.idiomatic: and defectors of fifth rank and below could be granted preferential appointments at once.

sentences.zh: 肅至義陽，頻破賊軍，除持節、都督、豫州刺史、揚州大中正。

translations.literal: Su reached Yiyang, repeatedly defeated enemy armies, and was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander, Governor of Yu Province, and Senior Rectifier of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Su reached Yiyang he repeatedly routed the enemy and was appointed bearer of the staff, area commander, governor of Yu Province, and senior rectifier of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 肅善撫接，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: Su was good at comforting and receiving people and had a very great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Su won people over with skillful care and soon enjoyed a wide reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋征入朝，帝手詔曰：「不見君子，中心如醉，一日三歲，我勞如何。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to court; the emperor wrote in his own hand: 'Not seeing the gentleman, the heart is as if drunk; one day like three years—how I toil!'
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to court. The emperor wrote in his own hand: 'Not to see the gentleman leaves the heart dizzy as with wine; one day is like three years—how I weary for you!

sentences.zh: 飾館華林，拂席相待，卿欲以何日發汝墳也？

translations.literal: I have adorned the lodge in the Flowery Grove and brushed the mat to await you—on what day do you wish to set out from your mound at Ru?'
translations.idiomatic: I have prepared the lodge in the Flowery Grove and brushed the mat in welcome—on what day will you set out from your post at Ru?'

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「蕭丁荼虣世，志等伍胥，窮逾再期，蔬縕不改。

translations.literal: ' Another edict said: 'The Xiao lad harms the age; his resolve equals Wu Zixu's; his hardship exceeds two years, yet coarse hemp is unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: ' Another edict read: 'The lad of the Xiao house ravages the realm; his resolve matches that of Wu Zixu; his mourning has run past the second year, yet he still wears his coarse hemp unchanged.

sentences.zh: 有司依禮喻解，為裁練禪之制。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices, following ritual, should admonish and release him, and set bounds for the transition from hemp to silk mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the proper offices, in accordance with ritual, urge him to end mourning and prescribe the change from hemp to silk.'

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，帝以久旱不雨輟膳，百寮詣闕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, because of long drought without rain the emperor ceased meals; the hundred officials went to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, prolonged drought led the emperor to stop taking meals, and the whole bureaucracy gathered at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 帝在崇虛樓，遣舍人問肅。

translations.literal: The emperor was in the Chongxu Tower and sent a palace attendant to question Su.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in the Chongxu Tower and sent a palace attendant to ask Su's view.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「伏承陛下輟膳，已經三日，群臣不敢自寧。

translations.literal: He replied: 'I humbly hear that Your Majesty has ceased meals for three days already; the ministers dare not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Su replied: 'I humbly learn that Your Majesty has abstained from food for three days already; the ministers dare not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯水湯旱，自定之數，須聖人以濟，未聞由聖以至災，是以國儲九年，以禦九年之變。

translations.literal: I have heard that Yao's flood and Tang's drought were numbers fixed of themselves; a sage is needed to bring relief—I have not heard that through a sage one reaches disaster; therefore the state stores nine years' grain to meet nine years' change.'
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the floods of Yao and the drought of Tang were ordained by fate and required a sage to remedy them; I have never heard that a sage brings disaster upon himself. That is why a state keeps nine years' grain in reserve against nine years of hardship.'

sentences.zh: 昨四郊之外已蒙滂澍，唯京城之內微為少澤。

translations.literal: Yesterday beyond the four suburbs there was already a soaking downpour; only within the capital was there slightly less moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the countryside beyond the four suburbs already received a soaking rain; only within the capital was the moisture somewhat slight.'

sentences.zh: 蒸庶未闕一攵食，陛下輟膳三日，臣庶惶惶，無復情地。

translations.literal: The common people have not lacked a single meal; Your Majesty has ceased meals three days—the ministers and people are in alarm and have no place for feeling.'
translations.idiomatic: The common people have not yet gone without a meal, yet Your Majesty has abstained for three days; officials and subjects alike are in dread and can find no peace of mind.'

sentences.zh: 」帝遣答曰：「雖不食數朝，猶然無感，朕誠心未至之所致也。

translations.literal: ' The emperor sent back answer: 'Though I have not eaten for several mornings, still there is no response—it is caused by my sincerity not yet reaching the mark.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor sent back his reply: 'Though I have gone without food for several mornings, heaven still does not respond; it must be because my sincerity has not yet been sufficient.

sentences.zh: 朕志確然，死而後已。

translations.literal: My resolve is firm; only death will end it.'
translations.idiomatic: My resolve is fixed; I shall not stop until death.'

sentences.zh: 」是夜，澍雨大降。

translations.literal: ' That night a great soaking rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: ' That night a torrential rain fell.

sentences.zh: 以破齊將裴叔業功，進號鎮南將軍，加都督四州諸軍事，封汝陽縣子。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating the Qi general Pei Shuye, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, with added command of all military affairs in four provinces, and he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating the Qi general Pei Shuye he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South, given overall command of military affairs in four provinces, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 肅頻表固讓，不許，詔加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Su repeatedly memorialized firmly declining; it was not permitted, and an edict added one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Su repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining the honors, but the court would not accept; an edict instead added a full set of martial music to his entourage.

sentences.zh: 初，齊之收肅父奐也，奐司馬黃瑤起攻奐殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qi seized Su's father Huan, Huan's Major Huang Yaoqi rose, attacked Huan, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qi arrested Su's father Huan, Huan's major Huang Yaoqi had risen against him, attacked him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年平漢陽，瑤起為輔國將軍，特詔以付肅，使紓泄哀情。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when Hanyang was pacified, Yaoqi was a General Who Assists the State; a special edict handed him over to Su to let grief be released.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, when Hanyang was pacified, Yaoqi was serving as General Who Assists the State; a special edict handed him over to Su so that Su might vent his grief.

sentences.zh: 孝文崩，遺詔以肅為尚書令，與咸陽王禧等同為宰輔，征會駕魯陽。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen died, the testamentary edict made Su Director of the Masters of Writing, equal with Prince Xianyang Xi and others as chief ministers, and summoned him to meet the imperial coffin at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen died, his final edict named Su Director of the Masters of Writing and made him a chief minister alongside Prince Xianyang of Xi and others, summoning him to join the funeral train at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 肅至，遂與禧參同謀謨。

translations.literal: When Su arrived, he then joined Xi in deliberating plans together.
translations.idiomatic: When Su arrived he took part with Xi in all major deliberations.

sentences.zh: 自魯陽至京洛，行途喪紀，委肅參量，憂勤經綜，有過舊戚。

translations.literal: From Luyang to Luoyang, mourning rites along the route were entrusted to Su to assess; his anxious diligence in overall arrangement exceeded old kin.
translations.idiomatic: From Luyang to Luoyang the funeral observances along the route were entrusted to Su for planning; his anxious diligence in managing every detail surpassed even the emperor's own kin.

sentences.zh: 禧兄弟並敬昵之，上下稱為和輯。

translations.literal: Xi and his brothers all respected and were intimate with him; above and below called it harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his brothers all treated him with respect and warmth, and court and princes alike praised the harmony among them.

sentences.zh: 唯任城王澄以其起自羈遠，一旦在己之上，每謂人曰：「朝廷以王肅加我上，尚可；

translations.literal: Only Prince Rencheng Cheng, because he rose from distant bonds and in a day was above himself, often said to people: 'For the court to place Wang Su above me is still tolerable;
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Rencheng of Cheng resented that a man who had come from a distant captive state should suddenly rank above him, and he often said: 'For the court to place Wang Su above me I can still accept;

sentences.zh: 從叔廣陵，宗室尊宿，歷任內外，云何一朝令肅居其右也？

translations.literal: my paternal uncle Guangling, a senior of the imperial clan who has served inside and outside—how in one morning can Su be set to his right?'
translations.idiomatic: but my uncle Guangling is a senior prince of the imperial house who has served at court and in the provinces for years—how can Su in a single day be set above him?'

sentences.zh: 」肅聞，恆降避之。

translations.literal: ' When Su heard, he always lowered himself and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: ' When Su heard this he always deferred to Cheng and kept out of his way.

sentences.zh: 尋為澄所奏劾，稱肅謀叛，事尋申釋。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached by Cheng, who said Su plotted rebellion; the matter was soon clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cheng impeached him on a charge of plotting rebellion, but the accusation was soon cleared.

sentences.zh: 詔肅尚陳留長公主，本劉昶子婦彭城公主也，賜錢二十萬、帛三千疋。

translations.literal: An edict married Su to the Princess Chang of Chenliu, originally daughter-in-law of Liu Chang the Princess of Pengcheng, and granted two hundred thousand cash and three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict married Su to the Princess Chang of Chenliu—formerly the wife of Liu Chang's son and known as the Princess of Pengcheng—and granted him two hundred thousand cash and three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 肅奏：「考以顯能，陟由績著升明退暗，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Su memorialized: 'Examination shows ability; promotion follows marked achievement, advancing the bright and retiring the dim—herein it lies.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized: 'Examinations reveal ability, promotions follow demonstrated achievement, and advancing the capable while retiring the incompetent depend on this principle.

sentences.zh: 自百寮曠察，四稔於茲，請依舊例，考檢能否。

translations.literal: Since the hundred officials have lacked inspection, four harvests have passed here; I request following the old precedent to examine and test ability.'
translations.idiomatic: The bureaucracy has gone without review for four years now; I ask that the old practice of assessing merit and competence be restored.'

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ' It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: ' The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業以壽春內附，拜肅使持節、都督江西諸軍事，與彭城王勰率步騎十萬以赴之。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye brought Shouchun over from within; Su was appointed Bearer of the Staff and Commander of all military affairs west of the river, and with Prince Pengcheng Xie led one hundred thousand foot and horse to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to Wei, Su was appointed bearer of the staff and commander of all military affairs west of the river, and marched with Prince Pengcheng of Xie at the head of a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 齊豫州刺史蕭懿屯小峴，交州刺史李叔獻屯合肥，將圖壽春。

translations.literal: Qi's Governor of Yu Xiao Yi encamped at Xiaoxian, Jiaozhou Governor Li Shuxian encamped at Hefei, intending to take Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's governor of Yu, Xiao Yi, encamped at Xiaoxian, and Jiaozhou governor Li Shuxian held Hefei, both intending to retake Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 肅進師討擊，大破之，禽叔獻，走蕭懿。

translations.literal: Su advanced the army to attack and greatly defeated them, captured Shuxian, and Xiao Yi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Su advanced to attack and routed them completely, capturing Li Shuxian while Xiao Yi fled.

sentences.zh: 還京師，宣武臨東堂，引見勞之，進位開府儀同三司，封昌國縣侯。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, Xuanwu received him in the Eastern Hall, summoned him for audience and consoled him, advanced him to Grand Preceptor with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital Emperor Xuanwu received him in the Eastern Hall, summoned him for audience and praised his service, promoted him to Grand Preceptor with the privileges of the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 尋為散騎常侍、都督淮南諸軍事、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, Commander of all military affairs in Huainan, and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed regular attendant, commander of all military affairs in Huainan, and governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 肅頻在邊，悉心撫接，遠近歸懷，附者若市，咸得其心。

translations.literal: Su was often on the frontier, devoted heart to comforting and receiving; near and far turned in allegiance, those attaching like a market—all won to his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Su spent long stretches on the frontier and devoted himself to winning people over; subjects near and far came to him in allegiance, newcomers crowding in like shoppers at a market, and he won them all.

sentences.zh: 清身好施，簡絕聲色，終始廉約，家無餘財。

translations.literal: He kept his person pure and loved giving; he was spare with sound and color; from start to finish he was frugal, and the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly, gave generously, shunned music and courtesans, and remained frugal to the end; his household held no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 然性微輕恌，頗以功名自許，護疵稱伐，少所推下，孝文每以此為言。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was slightly light and frivolous; he rather took merit and fame upon himself, shielded faults and proclaimed victories, and rarely deferred below—Xiaowen often spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was somewhat vain by nature, rather full of himself about his achievements, inclined to gloss over his faults and boast of his victories, and rarely deferential to others—a point Xiaowen often raised with him.

sentences.zh: 景明二年，薨于壽春，年三十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming he died at Shouchun, age thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingming reign (501) he died at Shouchun at the age of thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 宣武為舉哀，給東園秘器、朝服一襲、錢三十萬、帛一千疋、布五百疋、蠟三百斤，並問其卜遷遠近，專遣侍御史一人監護喪事。

translations.literal: Xuanwu performed mourning for him, supplied Eastern Garden secret vessels, one set of court dress, three hundred thousand cash, one thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, three hundred jin of wax, and also inquired about the divination for removal near or far, specially sending one attendant censor to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu mourned him in person and granted the full Eastern Garden funeral regalia, a set of court robes, three hundred thousand cash, one thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax; he also inquired about the auspices for the burial site and dispatched a dedicated attendant censor to supervise the rites.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「杜預之歿，窆于首陽，司空李沖，覆舟是托，顧瞻斯所，亦二代之九原也。

translations.literal: Another edict said: 'When Du Yu died he was buried at Shouyang; Minister of Works Li Chong entrusted his overturned boat—looking back on this place, it is also the Jiuyuan of two dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: 'When Du Yu died he was buried at Shouyang; when Minister of Works Li Chong passed away he chose this place for his final rest—gazing upon it, one sees the common graveyard of two dynasties.

sentences.zh: 故揚州刺史肅，忠義結於二世，英惠符于李、杜。

translations.literal: The former Governor of Yang Su bound loyalty and righteousness across two reigns; his heroic wisdom matched Li and Du.
translations.idiomatic: The late governor of Yang, Su, bound loyalty and righteousness across two reigns, and his brilliance matched that of Li Chong and Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 平生本意，願終京陵，既有宿心，宜遂先志。

translations.literal: His lifelong intent wished to end at the capital tombs; since he had this long-standing heart, his former will should be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he had wished to be buried in the capital cemetery; since that was his settled wish, let his former intent be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 其令葬於沖、預兩墳之間，使之神遊相得也。

translations.literal: Let him be buried between the two mounds of Chong and Yu, so their spirits wandering may meet.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him be buried between the tombs of Chong and Yu, that their spirits may keep company in the afterlife.'

sentences.zh: 」贈侍中、司空公。

translations.literal: ' He was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: ' He was posthumously appointed attendant-in-ordinary and Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 有司奏以肅貞心大度，宜諡匡公，詔諡宣簡。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Su's upright heart and great breadth suited the posthumous name Lord Who Rectifies; an edict gave the posthumous name Lord Who Proclaims Simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices proposed the posthumous title Lord Who Rectifies for his upright heart and magnanimity, but the edict instead granted Lord Who Proclaims Simplicity.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，詔為肅建碑銘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingdi's reign, an edict ordered a stele inscription built for Su.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign an edict ordered a memorial stele erected for Su.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏喪亂，禮樂崩亡，孝文雖厘革制度，變更風俗，其間樸略，未能淳也。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house's loss and disorder, ritual and music collapsed; though Xiaowen reformed systems and changed customs, amid them plainness and roughness could not yet be pure.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of the Jin, ritual and music had collapsed; though Xiaowen reformed institutions and changed customs, much remained rough and had not yet been refined.

sentences.zh: 肅明練舊事，虛心受委，朝儀國曲，咸自肅出。

translations.literal: Su was clear and practiced in old affairs, received commission with open heart; court ceremony and state ritual all came from Su.
translations.idiomatic: Su was thoroughly versed in ancient precedent and accepted every commission with humility; court ceremony and state ritual largely took shape through him.

sentences.zh: 子紹襲。

translations.literal: His son Shao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao inherited his titles.

sentences.zh: 紹字三歸，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Sangu, held the post of Secretariat Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, whose courtesy name was Sangu, served as vice-director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 子遷襲，齊受禪，爵隨例降。

translations.literal: His son Qian inherited; when Qi received the abdication, the rank followed precedent and was lowered.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian inherited the line; when Qi received the abdication of Wei, the family's rank was reduced in accordance with precedent.

sentences.zh: 紹弟理，孝靜初得還朝，位著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Li, at the beginning of Xiaojing was able to return to court and held the post of Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Li was able to return to court early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign and served as assistant in the Bureau of Composition.

sentences.zh: 紹，肅前妻謝生也。

translations.literal: Shao was born of Su's former wife, Lady Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie.

sentences.zh: 肅臨薨，謝始攜女及紹至壽春。

translations.literal: As Su was near death, Xie for the first time brought the daughter and Shao to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: When Su was dying, Lady Xie brought her daughter and Shao to Shouchun for the first time.

sentences.zh: 宣武納其女為夫人，明帝又納紹女為嬪。

translations.literal: Xuanwu took the daughter as Lady; Mingdi again took Shao's daughter as Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu took the daughter as his lady; Emperor Ming later took Shao's daughter as an imperial concubine.

sentences.zh: 肅弟康，字文政，涉獵書史，微有兄風。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Kang, styled Wenzheng, ranged through books and histories and had a slight trace of the elder brother's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Su's younger brother Kang, whose courtesy name was Wenzheng, read widely in books and histories and showed something of his elder brother's bearing.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，攜兄子誦、翊、衍等入魏，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, and Yan and others into Wei and was appointed Secretariat Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanwu's reign he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into Wei and was appointed vice-director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒幽州刺史，贈征虜將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of You Province; posthumously given General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as governor of You Province and was posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 誦字國章，肅長兄融之子。

translations.literal: Song, styled Guozhang, was son of Su's elder brother Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Song, whose courtesy name was Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.

sentences.zh: 學涉有文才，神氣清俊，風流甚美。

translations.literal: His learning ranged and he had literary talent; his spirit was clear and handsome, his elegance very fine.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and gifted as a writer; his bearing was clear and refined, and his elegance was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 歷位散騎常侍、光祿大夫、右將軍、幽州刺史、長兼秘書監、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through posts as Regular Attendant, Grand Master for the Glorious, General of the Right, Governor of You Province, Concurrent Long-term Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Attendant at the Yellow Gate within the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of regular attendant, grand master for the glorious, general of the right, governor of You Province, concurrent supervisor of the secretariat, and attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，靈太后之立幼主也，于時大赦。

translations.literal: When Mingdi died and Empress Dowager Ling established the young lord, at that time there was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died and Empress Dowager Ling installed the young emperor, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 誦宣讀詔書，言制抑揚，風神竦秀，百寮傾屬，莫不歎美。

translations.literal: Song proclaimed and read the edict; his words rose and fell with restraint, his bearing lofty and fine; the hundred officials leaned toward him, all sighing in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Song read the amnesty edict aloud; his delivery rose and fell with perfect control, his presence lofty and striking, and the entire bureaucracy watched in admiration.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，于河陰遇害，贈尚書左僕射、司空公，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he met harm at Heyin; posthumously given Left Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Works, posthumous name Lord Who Proclaims Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin and was posthumously appointed left vice-director of the masters of writing and Duke of Works, with the posthumous title Lord Who Proclaims Culture.

sentences.zh: 子孝康，尚書郎中。

translations.literal: His son Xiaokang was a Master of Writing Lang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaokang served as a master of writing lang.

sentences.zh: 孝康弟俊賦，性清雅，頗有文才，齊文襄王中外府祭酒。

translations.literal: Xiaokang's younger brother Junfu was by nature pure and elegant, with considerable literary talent, Libationer of the Central and Outer Office of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokang's younger brother Junfu was refined and retiring by nature, showed considerable literary talent, and served as libationer in the central and outer office of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 誦弟衍，字文舒，名行器藝亞於誦。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Yan, styled Wenshu, in fame, conduct, talent, and craft was second to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Yan, whose courtesy name was Wenshu, was slightly below Song in reputation, conduct, and ability.

sentences.zh: 位光祿大夫、廷尉卿、揚州刺史、大中正、度支七兵二尚書、太常卿。

translations.literal: He held posts as Grand Master for the Glorious, Director of the Court of Justice, Governor of Yang Province, Senior Rectifier, Director of the Masters of Writing for Revenue and the Seven Armies, and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand master for the glorious, director of the court of justice, governor of Yang Province, senior rectifier, director of the masters of writing for revenue and the seven armies, and director of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Regular Attendant and Governor of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as regular attendant and governor of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 為爾硃仲遠所禽，以其名望，不害。

translations.literal: He was captured by Erzhu Zhongyuan; because of his fame and standing, he was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He was captured by Erzhu Zhongyuan, who spared his life out of respect for his reputation.

sentences.zh: 令騎牛從軍，久乃見釋遠洛。

translations.literal: He was made to ride an ox with the army; only after long time was he released to return far to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made to ride an ox with the army and was not released to return to Luoyang until much later.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，位侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he served as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 卒，敕給東園秘器，贈尚書令、司徒公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: He died; an edict granted Eastern Garden secret vessels; posthumously given Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Masses, posthumous name Lord Who Proclaims Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He died; an edict granted the Eastern Garden funeral regalia; he was posthumously appointed director of the masters of writing and Duke of the Masses, with the posthumous title Lord Who Proclaims Documents.

sentences.zh: 衍篤於交舊。

translations.literal: Yan was earnest toward friends of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was deeply loyal to old friends.

sentences.zh: 有故人竺ＩＱ，於西兗州為仲遠所害，其妻子饑寒，衍置於家，累年贍恤，世人稱其敦厚。

translations.literal: He had an old friend Zhu [IQ], who at Western Yan Province was killed by Zhongyuan; his wife and children were hungry and cold; Yan placed them in his home and for successive years supported and comforted them—the world praised his generous solidity.
translations.idiomatic: An old friend of his named Zhu [IQ] had been killed by Zhongyuan while serving in Western Yan Province; when the man's wife and children were left hungry and cold, Yan took them into his household and supported them for years, earning wide praise for his steadfast kindness.

sentences.zh: 翊字士遊，肅次兄深子也。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Shiyou, was Su's second elder brother Shen's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Shiyou, was the son of Shen, Su's second elder brother.

sentences.zh: 風神秀立，好學有文才。

translations.literal: His bearing and spirit were elegant and upright; he loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was graceful in bearing and upright in spirit, loved learning, and possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Palace Writer Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a palace writer attendant.

sentences.zh: 頗銳于榮利，結婚於元叉。

translations.literal: He was quite keen on glory and profit and formed a marriage alliance with Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather eager for rank and profit and entered into a marriage alliance with Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 為濟州刺史，清靜有政績。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Ji Province, governing with quiet purity and achieving administrative merit.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Ji Province he governed with quiet integrity and won a record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary of Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master for the Glorious with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently served as Director of the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry and grand master for the glorious with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and concurrently served as director of the national academy.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Duke of the Minister of Works and Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Duke of the Minister of Works and governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 子琛，武定中，儀同、開府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Chen, in the Wuding period, held the posts of Pillar of State and Staff Officer of the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen, during the Wuding era, served as pillar of state and staff officer of the opening office.

sentences.zh: 劉芳，字伯支，彭城叢亭里人，漢楚元王交之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, styled Bozhi, was a man of Congting Lane in Pengcheng and a descendant of Jiao, Prince Yuan of Chu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, whose courtesy name was Bozhi, came from Congting Lane in Pengcheng and was a descendant of Jiao, Prince Yuan of Chu of the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 六世祖訥，晉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Ne served as Jin Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Ne had served as colonel director of retainers under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖該，宋青、徐二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gai was Governor of the two provinces of Qing and Xu under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gai had served as governor of Qing and Xu provinces under Song.

sentences.zh: 父邕，宋兗州長史。

translations.literal: His father Yong was Chief Administrator of Yan Province under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong had served as chief administrator of Yan Province under Song.

sentences.zh: 芳出後宋東平太守遜之。

translations.literal: Fang was made heir to Xunzhi, Governor of Dongping under Song.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was adopted as heir to Xunzhi, who had served as governor of Dongping under Song.

sentences.zh: 邕同劉義宣之事，身死彭城。

translations.literal: Yong joined Liu Yixuan's affair and died at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong took part in Liu Yixuan's rebellion and was killed at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 芳隨伯母房逃竄清州，會赦免。

translations.literal: Fang fled with his father's elder brother's wife Fang to Qing Province and was pardoned when an amnesty was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fled with his aunt Fang to Qing Province and was spared when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 舅元慶，為宋青州刺史沈文秀建威府司馬，為文秀所殺。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Yuan Qing served as Major of the Establishing Might Office of Song Governor of Qing Province Shen Wenxiu and was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Yuan Qing had served as major in the Establishing Might office of Shen Wenxiu, governor of Qing Province under Song, and was killed by Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 芳母子入梁鄒城。

translations.literal: Fang and his mother entered Liangzou city.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his mother took refuge in Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜南討青、齊，梁鄒降，芳北徙為平齊人，時年十六。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao marched south to attack Qing and Qi; Liangzou surrendered; Fang was moved north and became a man of Pingqi; he was then sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao marched south against Qing and Qi and Liangzou surrendered, Fang was resettled in the north and became a subject of Pingqi; he was sixteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 南部尚書李敷妻，司徒崔浩之弟女，芳祖母，浩之姑也。

translations.literal: The wife of Minister of the Southern Branch Li Fu was the daughter of Minister of Works Cui Hao's younger brother; she was Fang's grandmother and Hao's paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, minister of the southern branch, had married the daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother; she was Fang's grandmother and Hao's paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 芳至京師，詣敷門。

translations.literal: When Fang reached the capital he went to Fu's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang reached the capital he went to Li Fu's house.

sentences.zh: 崔恥芳流播，拒不見之。

translations.literal: The Cui clan were ashamed of Fang's wandering exile and refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The Cui family were ashamed that Fang had been cast adrift in exile and refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 芳雖處窮窘之中，而業尚貞固。

translations.literal: Although Fang was in extreme want, his pursuit remained steadfast and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Though Fang lived in utter poverty, he held fast to his principles.

sentences.zh: 聰敏過人，篤志墳典，晝則亻庸書以自資給，夜則誦經不寢。

translations.literal: His intelligence surpassed others; he devoted himself to the classics of the ancients; by day he hired out his copying to support himself, and by night he recited the classics without sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted beyond ordinary men, he devoted himself to the classics of antiquity; by day he copied texts for hire to support himself, and by night he recited scripture without rest.

sentences.zh: 至有易衣亻並日之弊，而淡然自守，不急急於榮利，不戚戚於貧賤，乃著《窮通論》以自慰。

translations.literal: He even came to the hardship of changing clothes on alternate days, yet he calmly kept himself intact, not urgently seeking glory and profit, not grieving over poverty and low station, and therefore wrote the 《On Fortune and Misfortune》 to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: At times he could afford only to change clothes on alternate days, yet he remained calmly self-possessed, neither grasping after rank and profit nor brooding over poverty and obscurity, and wrote the 《On Fortune and Misfortune》 to console himself.

sentences.zh: 常為諸僧亻庸寫經論，筆跡稱善，卷直一縑，歲中能入百餘疋。

translations.literal: He regularly copied sutras and treatises for hire for various monks; his handwriting was praised as excellent; one scroll fetched one bolt of silk, and in a year he could earn more than a hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly copied sutras and treatises for monks on commission; his calligraphy was highly praised, each scroll bringing one bolt of silk, and in a year he could earn more than a hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，賴以頗振。

translations.literal: After several years like this, he relied on it to recover considerably.
translations.idiomatic: After several years of this work his circumstances improved considerably.

sentences.zh: 由是與德學大僧多有還往。

translations.literal: From this he had much coming and going with great monks of virtue and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Through this he came to associate with many eminent monks of virtue and learning.

sentences.zh: 時有南方沙門慧度以事被責，未幾暴亡，芳因緣聞知。

translations.literal: At the time there was a southern monk named Huidu who was punished for an affair; before long he died suddenly, and Fang learned of it through connections.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a southern monk named Huidu was punished for some offense; he soon died suddenly, and Fang came to hear of it through his connections.

sentences.zh: 文明太后召入禁中，鞭之一百。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned him into the inner palace and gave him a hundred lashes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned him into the inner palace and had him flogged a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 時中官李豐主其始末，知芳篤學有志行，言之于太后。

translations.literal: At the time the palace eunuch Li Feng was in charge of the whole affair; knowing Fang's earnest learning and aspiration and conduct, he spoke of it to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Li Feng, who was in charge of the case, knew of Fang's devoted scholarship and upright character and reported this to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 微愧於心。

translations.literal: She felt slight shame in her heart.
translations.idiomatic: She felt a twinge of remorse.

sentences.zh: 會齊使劉纘至，芳之始族兄也，擢芳兼主客郎，與纘相接。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qi envoy Liu Zhuan arrived; he was Fang's elder clansman of the first generation, and Fang was promoted to Acting Master of Guests and received Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi envoy Liu Zhuan arrived—Fang's elder clansman—Fang was promoted to acting master of guests and received Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 拜中書博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Writer Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed palace writer erudite.

sentences.zh: 後與崔光、宋弁、刑產等俱為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he served together with Cui Guang, Song Bian, Xing Chan, and others as Palace Writer Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served together with Cui Guang, Song Bian, Xing Chan, and others as palace writer attendant.

sentences.zh: 俄而詔芳與產入授皇太子經，遷太子庶子，兼員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Fang and Chan to enter and instruct the Crown Prince in the classics; he was transferred to Crown Prince Household Mentor and concurrently made Acting Attendant-in-Ordinary of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Fang and Xing Chan to instruct the crown prince in the classics; Fang was transferred to crown prince household mentor and concurrently made acting attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從駕洛陽，自在路及旋京師，恆侍坐講讀。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial progress to Luoyang; from the road onward and on the return to the capital he constantly sat in attendance lecturing and reading.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Luoyang and, both on the journey and on the return to the capital, constantly sat in attendance lecturing and reading with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 芳才思深敏，特精經義，博聞強記，兼覽《蒼雅》，尤長音訓，辯析無疑。

translations.literal: Fang's talent and thought were deep and keen; he was especially expert in the meaning of the classics, broadly learned with a strong memory, and also read the 《Cangya》; he was especially skilled in pronunciation and glosses and analyzed without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's mind was deep and quick; he was especially expert in classical exegesis, broadly learned with a prodigious memory, and also mastered the 《Cangya》; he excelled above all in pronunciation and glosses and could analyze points without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 於是禮遇日隆，賞賚豐渥。

translations.literal: Thereupon his ceremonial treatment grew daily more exalted and his rewards and gifts rich and generous.
translations.idiomatic: His honors grew daily, and his rewards became ever more lavish.

sentences.zh: 俄兼通直常侍，從駕南巡，撰述行事，尋而除正。

translations.literal: Before long he was concurrently made Acting Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary; he accompanied the imperial progress on the southern tour and compiled accounts of the journey; soon afterward he was given the regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting direct attendant-in-ordinary, accompanied the emperor on the southern tour, and compiled an account of the journey; shortly afterward he received the regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 王肅之來奔也，孝文雅相器重，朝野屬目。

translations.literal: When Wang Su came over in flight, Emperor Xiaowen greatly valued him in person, and court and countryside fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su defected to the north, Emperor Xiaowen held him in high personal esteem, and all eyes in court and countryside were upon him.

sentences.zh: 芳未及相見。

translations.literal: Fang had not yet met him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had not yet met him.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴群臣于華林，肅語次云：「古者唯婦人有笄，男子則無笄。

translations.literal: Once, feasting the ministers at Hualin, Su said in the course of conversation: 'In antiquity only women had hairpins; men had none.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while feasting the ministers at Hualin, Su remarked in conversation: 'In antiquity only women wore hairpins; men did not.

sentences.zh: 」芳曰：「推經《禮》正文，古者男子婦人俱有笄。

translations.literal: ' Fang said: 'Extrapolating from the main text of the 《Rites》, in antiquity both men and women had hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: ' Fang replied: 'If one extrapolates from the main text of the 《Rites》, in antiquity both men and women wore hairpins.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「《喪服》稱男子免而婦人髽，男子冠而婦人笄，如此則男子不應有笄。

translations.literal: ' Su said: 'The 《Mourning Dress》 says that men remove their caps while women wear mourning buns, and men don caps while women wear hairpins—if so, men ought not to have hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: ' Su said: 'The 《Mourning Dress》 states that when men remove their caps women wear mourning buns, and when men don caps women wear hairpins—by this reasoning men ought not to wear hairpins.

sentences.zh: 」芳曰：「此專謂凶事也。

translations.literal: ' Fang said: 'This speaks exclusively of inauspicious affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ' Fang said: 'That passage refers exclusively to mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：初遭喪，男子免，時則婦人髽；

translations.literal: The 《Rites》: when one first encounters mourning, the man removes his cap, and at that time the woman wears a mourning bun;
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites》 says: when mourning first begins, the man removes his cap, and at that time the woman wears a mourning bun;

sentences.zh: 男子冠，時則婦人笄。

translations.literal: when the man dons his cap, at that time the woman wears a hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: when the man dons his cap, at that time the woman wears a hairpin.

sentences.zh: 言俱時變，男子婦人免髽、冠笄之不同也。

translations.literal: It means that both change at the same time—the difference between men and women in removing caps and wearing buns, and donning caps and wearing hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: The text means that both change at the same time—it describes the different mourning forms for men and women: removing caps and wearing buns, and donning caps and wearing hairpins.

sentences.zh: 又冠尊，故奪其笄，且互言也。

translations.literal: Moreover the cap is higher in rank, so the hairpin is set aside, and moreover the phrasing is reciprocal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because the cap outranks the hairpin, the hairpin is set aside, and the phrasing is deliberately reciprocal.

sentences.zh: 非謂男子無笄。

translations.literal: It does not mean that men have no hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: It does not mean that men wore no hairpins.

sentences.zh: 又《禮內則》稱：'子事父母，雞初鳴，櫛纚笄總。

translations.literal: Moreover the 《Inner Rules of the Rites》 says: 'When a son serves his parents, at the first crow of the cock he combs his hair, ties it, inserts his hairpin, and gathers it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the 《Inner Rules of the Rites》 states: 'When a son serves his parents, at the first crow of the cock he combs his hair, ties it, inserts his hairpin, and gathers it.

sentences.zh: '以茲而言，男子有笄明矣。

translations.literal: ' From this speaking, it is clear that men had hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: ' From this it is clear that men wore hairpins.

sentences.zh: 」高祖稱善者久之。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Xiaowen praised it as good for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: ' Emperor Xiaowen praised the argument at length.

sentences.zh: 肅亦以芳言為然，曰：「此非劉石經也？

translations.literal: Su also took Fang's words as correct and said: 'Is this not Liu the Stone Classics expert?
translations.idiomatic: Su also accepted Fang's argument and said: 'Is this not Liu the Stone Classics expert?

sentences.zh: 」昔漢世造三字石經于太學，學者文字不正，多往質焉。

translations.literal: ' In former times the Han dynasty carved the Three-Character Stone Classics at the Imperial University; when scholars' written characters were incorrect, many went to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: ' In Han times the Three-Character Stone Classics were carved at the Imperial University; whenever scholars were uncertain about written characters, many went to consult the expert.

sentences.zh: 芳音義明辯，疑者皆往詢訪，故時人號為劉石經。

translations.literal: Fang's pronunciation and meaning were clear and discriminating; those in doubt all went to inquire of him, and therefore people of the time called him Liu the Stone Classics expert.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's explanations of pronunciation and meaning were lucid and precise; all who were in doubt came to consult him, and people of the time called him Liu the Stone Classics expert.

sentences.zh: 酒闌，芳與肅俱出。

translations.literal: When the wine was nearly finished, Fang and Su both went out.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet drew to a close, Fang and Su left together.

sentences.zh: 肅執芳手曰：「吾少來留意《三禮》，在南諸儒，亟共討論，皆謂此義，如吾向言。

translations.literal: Su took Fang's hand and said: 'From youth I have attended to the 《Three Rites》; with the scholars of the south I repeatedly discussed this together, and all said this meaning was as I said earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Su took Fang's hand and said: 'From youth I have devoted myself to the 《Three Rites》; with the southern scholars I discussed this point again and again, and all agreed with what I said earlier.

sentences.zh: 今聞往釋，頓祛平生之惑。

translations.literal: Now hearing your explanation, I have suddenly dispelled the doubts of a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Now, hearing your explanation, a lifelong doubt has been swept away at once.

sentences.zh: 」芳理義精贍，類皆如是。

translations.literal: ' Fang's reasoning and meaning were refined and ample; cases were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: ' Fang's reasoning was always as thorough and precise as this.

sentences.zh: 孝文遷洛，路由朝歌，見殷比干墓，愴然悼懷，為文以吊之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, the route passed Chaoge; he saw the tomb of Bi Gan of Yin, was deeply moved with grief, and composed a text to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, the route passed Chaoge; seeing the tomb of Bi Gan of Yin, he was deeply moved and composed a text to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 芳為注解，表上之。

translations.literal: Fang wrote annotations and submitted them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Fang wrote annotations and submitted them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「覽卿注，殊為富博。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Having read your annotations, they are exceptionally rich and broad.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: 'Having read your annotations, I find them exceptionally rich and comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 但文非屈、宋，理慚張、賈。

translations.literal: But the writing is not that of Qu Yuan and Song Yu, and the reasoning falls short of Zhang Yi and Jia Yi.
translations.idiomatic: But the prose does not match Qu Yuan and Song Yu, and the reasoning falls short of Zhang Yi and Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 既有雅致，便可付之集書。

translations.literal: Since it already has refined elegance, it may be entrusted to the compilation office.
translations.idiomatic: Since it already has refined elegance, it may be entrusted to the compilation office.

sentences.zh: 」詔以芳經學精洽，超遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: ' An edict, because Fang's classical learning was refined and thorough, promoted him beyond regular rank to Director of the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: ' An edict, recognizing Fang's mastery of classical learning, promoted him beyond regular rank to director of the national academy.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 夫為國家者罔不崇儒尊道，學校為先。

translations.literal: Those who govern a state none fail to exalt Confucianism and honor the Way, putting schools first.
translations.idiomatic: Those who govern a state invariably exalt Confucian learning and honor the Way, putting schools first.

sentences.zh: 唐虞以往，典籍無據；

translations.literal: From the age of Tang and Yu onward, the classics offer no evidence;
translations.idiomatic: From the age of Tang and Yu onward, the classics offer no clear evidence;

sentences.zh: 隆周以降，任居武門。

translations.literal: from flourishing Zhou downward, the office was located at the Martial Gate.
translations.idiomatic: but from flourishing Zhou downward, the office was located at the Martial Gate.

sentences.zh: 蔡氏《勸學篇》云：「周之師氏居武門左。

translations.literal: Cai's 《Exhortation to Learning》 says: 'Zhou's Master Teacher dwelt to the left of the Martial Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Cai's 《Exhortation to Learning》 states: 'Zhou's master teacher dwelt to the left of the Martial Gate.

sentences.zh: 」今之祭酒則周師氏。

translations.literal: ' The present Director of the National Academy is thus Zhou's Master Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: ' The present director of the national academy corresponds to Zhou's master teacher.

sentences.zh: 《洛陽記》：「國子學宮與天子宮對。

translations.literal: The 《Record of Luoyang》: 'The National Academy's school palace faced the Son of Heaven's palace.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Record of Luoyang》 says: 'The national academy's school palace faced the Son of Heaven's palace.

sentences.zh: 太學在開陽門外。

translations.literal: The Imperial University was outside the Kaiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial university stood outside the Kaiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 」案《學記》云：「古之王者，建國親人，教學為先。

translations.literal: ' Examining the 《Record of Learning》, it says: 'The ancient kings, in founding a state and cherishing the people, put teaching and learning first.
translations.idiomatic: ' Examining the 《Record of Learning》, it says: 'The ancient kings, in founding a state and cherishing the people, put teaching and learning first.

sentences.zh: 」鄭氏注：「內則設師保以教，使國子學焉；

translations.literal: ' Zheng's commentary: 'Within, masters and protectors were established to teach, causing the sons of the state to study there;
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng's commentary explains: 'Within the palace, masters and protectors were established to teach, and the sons of the state studied there;

sentences.zh: 外則有太學庠序之官。

translations.literal: without, there were the officials of the Imperial University and the village schools.
translations.idiomatic: outside the palace were the officials of the imperial university and the village schools.

sentences.zh: 」由斯而言，國學在內，太學在外，明矣。

translations.literal: ' From this speaking, the National Academy was within and the Imperial University without—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: ' From this it is clear that the national academy lay within the palace and the imperial university without.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今既徙縣崧瀍，皇居伊洛，宮闕府寺，僉復故址，至於國學，豈宜舛錯？

translations.literal: Your subject holds that now, having moved the county to Song and Chan, with the imperial residence at Yi and Luo, palaces, gates, and government offices all restored to their former sites, as for the National Academy, how can it be placed amiss?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that now, with the capital moved to the Song and Chan region and the imperial residence established at Luoyang, palaces and government offices have all been restored to their proper sites—how then can the national academy be placed incorrectly?

sentences.zh: 校量舊事，應在宮門之左。

translations.literal: Weighing the old precedents, it should be to the left of the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the old precedents, it should stand to the left of the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 至如太學，基所見存，仍舊營構。

translations.literal: As for the Imperial University, the foundations that I have seen still exist and should be built upon as before.
translations.idiomatic: As for the imperial university, the foundations I have seen still remain and should be rebuilt on the old site.

sentences.zh: 又云太初太和二十年，發敕立四門博士，于四門置學。

translations.literal: It also says that in the twentieth year of Taihe of the Taichu reign, an edict was issued to establish Four-Gate Erudites and to set up schools at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: It also records that in the twentieth year of Taihe, during the Taichu reign, an edict established four-gate erudites and founded schools at the four gates.

sentences.zh: 臣案：自周已上，學唯以二，或尚東，或尚西，或貴在國，或貴在郊。

translations.literal: Your subject investigates: from Zhou upward, schools numbered only two; some honored the east, some the west, some valued those within the capital, some those in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject finds that from Zhou upward schools numbered only two; some honored the east, some the west, some valued those within the capital, and some those in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 爰暨周室，學蓋有六：師氏居內，太學在國，四小在效。

translations.literal: Down to the Zhou house, schools altogether numbered six: the Master Teacher dwelt within, the Imperial University was in the capital, and the four lesser schools were in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhou dynasty schools altogether numbered six: the master teacher dwelt within the palace, the imperial university stood in the capital, and the four lesser schools lay in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 《禮記云：「周人養庶老于虞庠，虞庠在國之四郊。

translations.literal: The 《Record of Rites》 says: 'The Zhou people nourished the common aged at the Yu school, and the Yu school was in the four suburbs of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Record of Rites》 says: 'The Zhou people nourished the common aged at the Yu school, and the Yu school stood in the four suburbs of the capital.

sentences.zh: 」《禮》又云：「天子設四學，當入學而太子齒。

translations.literal: ' The 《Rites》 also says: 'The Son of Heaven established four schools; when he entered school the Crown Prince took his place by age.
translations.idiomatic: ' The 《Rites》 also says: 'The Son of Heaven established four schools; when he entered school the crown prince took his place according to age.

sentences.zh: 」注云：「四學，周四郊之虞庠也。

translations.literal: ' The commentary says: 'The four schools were the Yu schools in the four suburbs of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: ' The commentary explains: 'The four schools were the Yu schools in the four suburbs of the capital.

sentences.zh: 」《大戴·保傅篇》云：「帝入東學，尚親而貴仁；

translations.literal: ' The 《Da Dai · Protector and Tutor》 chapter says: 'The Emperor entered the Eastern School, honoring kinship and valuing benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: ' The 《Da Dai · Protector and Tutor》 chapter says: 'The emperor entered the eastern school, honoring kinship and valuing benevolence;

sentences.zh: 帝入南學，尚齒而貴信；

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Southern School, honoring age and valuing trustworthiness;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor entered the southern school, honoring age and valuing trustworthiness;

sentences.zh: 帝入西學，尚賢而貴德；

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Western School, honoring worth and valuing virtue;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor entered the western school, honoring worth and valuing virtue;

sentences.zh: 帝入北學，尚貴而尊爵；

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Northern School, honoring rank and revering titles;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor entered the northern school, honoring rank and revering titles;

sentences.zh: 帝入太學，承師而問道。

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Imperial University, receiving teachers and inquiring into the Way.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor entered the imperial university, receiving teachers and inquiring into the Way.

sentences.zh: 」周之五學，於此彌彰。

translations.literal: ' Zhou's five schools are here made all the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zhou's five schools are here made all the clearer.

sentences.zh: 案鄭注《學記》，周則六學，所以然者，注云：「內則設師保以教，使國子學焉；

translations.literal: Examining Zheng's commentary on the 《Record of Learning》, under Zhou there were six schools; the reason is that the commentary says: 'Within, masters and protectors were established to teach, causing the sons of the state to study there;
translations.idiomatic: Examining Zheng's commentary on the 《Record of Learning》, under Zhou there were six schools; the reason, as the commentary explains, is that 'within the palace, masters and protectors were established to teach, and the sons of the state studied there;

sentences.zh: 外則有太學庠序之官。

translations.literal: without, there were the officials of the Imperial University and the village schools.
translations.idiomatic: outside the palace were the officials of the imperial university and the village schools.

sentences.zh: 」此其證也。

translations.literal: ' This is its proof.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is the evidence for it.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏已降，無復四郊。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei downward, there were no longer four suburban districts.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei downward, the four suburban districts no longer existed.

sentences.zh: 謹尋先旨，宜在四門。

translations.literal: Respectfully tracing the earlier intent, they should be at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully tracing the earlier intent, the schools should be placed at the four gates.

sentences.zh: 案王肅注云：「天子四郊有學，去都五十里。

translations.literal: Examining Wang Su's commentary, it says: 'The Son of Heaven had schools in the four suburbs, fifty li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's commentary states: 'The Son of Heaven had schools in the four suburbs, fifty li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 」考之鄭氏，不雲遠近。

translations.literal: ' Examining Zheng's school, it does not speak of distance.
translations.idiomatic: ' Examining Zheng's commentary, it says nothing about distance.

sentences.zh: 今太學故坊，基址寬曠。

translations.literal: Now the former site of the Imperial University -- the foundation is broad and spacious.
translations.idiomatic: The former site of the imperial university has a broad and spacious foundation.

sentences.zh: 四郊別置，相去遼闊，檢督難周。

translations.literal: If set separately in the four suburbs, the distance between them is vast and remote, and inspection and supervision are hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Placing them separately in the four suburbs would leave them far apart, making inspection and supervision difficult to carry out fully.

sentences.zh: 計太學坊並作四門，猶為太曠。

translations.literal: Even counting the Imperial University precinct together with making the four gates, it is still too spacious.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the imperial university precinct and all four gate schools were combined, the space would still be too large.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚量，同處無嫌。

translations.literal: By this subject's foolish reckoning, sharing one place would be without objection.
translations.idiomatic: In this official's humble view, there would be no objection to placing them in the same location.

sentences.zh: 且今時制置，多循中代，未審四學應從古不？

translations.literal: Moreover, the present arrangements mostly follow the middle dynasties; it is not yet clear whether the four schools should follow antiquity or not?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, current arrangements largely follow the middle dynasties, and it is unclear whether the four schools should follow ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 求集儒禮官議其定所。

translations.literal: Request that Confucian and ritual officials be assembled to discuss the fixed location.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Confucian scholars and ritual officials be convened to decide on a fixed location.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; Chancellor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 出除青州刺史。

translations.literal: He left the capital and was appointed Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to take up the post of Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 為政儒緩，不能禁止奸盜；

translations.literal: In governing he was Confucian and lenient and could not prohibit villainy and banditry;
translations.idiomatic: His governance was scholarly and lenient, and he proved unable to suppress crime and banditry;

sentences.zh: 然廉清寡欲，無撓公私。

translations.literal: yet he was incorrupt, pure, and of few desires, and did not disturb public or private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was incorruptible and moderate in his desires, interfering neither with public affairs nor with private interests.

sentences.zh: 還朝，議定律令。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he deliberated on fixing statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court, he took part in deliberations to codify statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 芳斟酌古今，為大議之主，其中損益，多芳意也。

translations.literal: Fang weighed ancient and modern, serving as master of the great deliberation; the additions and subtractions within it were largely Fang's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Fang weighed ancient and modern practice and served as the chief architect of the great deliberation; most of the revisions reflected his own views.

sentences.zh: 宣武以朝儀多闕，其一切諸議悉委芳修正，於是朝廷吉凶大事，皆就諮訪焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, because court ritual had many omissions, entrusted to Fang the correction of all such deliberations; henceforth for the court's auspicious and inauspicious great affairs, all were consulted through inquiry to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because court ritual contained many gaps, Emperor Xuanwu entrusted Fang with revising all such deliberations, and thereafter the court sought his counsel on all major state ceremonies, auspicious or otherwise.

sentences.zh: 轉太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 芳以所置五郊及日月之位，去城里數於《禮》有違；

translations.literal: Fang, because the positions established for the five suburban sacrifices and for the sun and moon, in the number of li from the city, violated the 《Rites》;
translations.idiomatic: Fang held that the locations established for the five suburban altars and for the sun and moon sacrifices, in their distance from the city in li, violated the requirements of the 《Rites》;

sentences.zh: 又靈星、周公之祀，不應隸太常，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Also, the sacrifices to the Spirit Star and to the Duke of Zhou ought not to be subordinate to the Ministry of Rites, and so he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He further argued that sacrifices to the Spirit Star and to the Duke of Zhou should not fall under the Ministry of Rites, and submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國之大事，莫先郊祀；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that among the great affairs of the state, none comes before suburban sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that among the great affairs of state, none takes precedence over suburban sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 郊祀之本，實在審位。

translations.literal: The root of suburban sacrifice lies truly in examining position.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of suburban sacrifice lies in determining the correct locations.

sentences.zh: 臣學謝全經，業乖通古，豈可輕薦瞽言，妄陳管說！

translations.literal: Your subject's learning falls short of mastering the complete classics, my craft strays from penetrating antiquity -- how could I lightly offer a blind man's words and rashly set forth narrow views!
translations.idiomatic: My learning falls short of a complete mastery of the classics, and my craft lacks full penetration of antiquity -- how could I lightly offer the words of a blind man or rashly advance narrow opinions!

sentences.zh: 竊見所置壇祠，遠近之宜，考之典制，或未允衷，既曰職司，請陳膚淺。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that the altars and shrines established, in the fitness of their distance, examined against canonical institutions, may not satisfy the heart; since this is my official charge, I beg to set forth superficial views.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that the distances at which the established altars and shrines are placed may not, when checked against canonical institutions, be entirely satisfactory; as this falls within my official responsibilities, I beg leave to offer these preliminary views.

sentences.zh: 《孟春令》云：「其數八。

translations.literal: The 《First Month of Spring Ordinance》 says: 「Its number is eight.
translations.idiomatic: The 《First Month of Spring Ordinance》 states: 「Its number is eight.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「迎春於東郊。

translations.literal: 」 It also says: 「Welcome spring in the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 」 It also says: 「Welcome spring in the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 」盧植云：「東郊，八里郊也。

translations.literal: 」 Lu Zhi says: 「The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Lu Zhi writes: 「The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 」賈逵云：「東郊，木帝太昊，八里。

translations.literal: 」 Jia Kui says: 「The eastern suburb is the Wood Emperor Tai Hao, eight li.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Jia Kui writes: 「The eastern suburb belongs to the Wood Emperor Tai Hao, eight li away.

sentences.zh: 」許慎云：「東郊，八里郊也。

translations.literal: 」 Xu Shen says: 「The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Xu Shen writes: 「The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄《孟春令》注云：「王居明堂。

translations.literal: 」 Zheng Xuan's commentary on the 《First Month of Spring Ordinance》 says: 「The king dwells in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Zheng Xuan's commentary on the 《First Month of Spring Ordinance》 states: 「The king dwells in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「王出十五里迎歲。

translations.literal: The 《Rites》 say: 「The king goes out fifteen li to welcome the year.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites》 state: 「The king goes out fifteen li to welcome the year.

sentences.zh: 」蓋殷禮也。

translations.literal: 」 This was the rite of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: 」 This was the ritual of the Yin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 周禮，近郊五十里。

translations.literal: In Zhou ritual, the near suburb was fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou ritual, the near suburban altar lay fifty li away.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄別注云：「東郊去都城八里。

translations.literal: 」 Zheng Xuan's separate commentary says: 「The eastern suburb is eight li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Zheng Xuan's separate commentary states: 「The eastern suburban altar is eight li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 」高誘云：「迎春氣於東方，八里郊也。

translations.literal: 」 Gao You says: 「Welcoming spring qi in the east, the eight-li suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Gao You writes: 「Welcoming the breath of spring in the east, at the eight-li suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 」王肅云：「東郊八里，因木數也。

translations.literal: 」 Wang Su says: 「The eastern suburb, eight li, following the number of wood.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Wang Su writes: 「The eastern suburb lies eight li away, in accordance with the number associated with wood.

sentences.zh: 」此皆同謂春郊八里之明據也。

translations.literal: 」 All alike clearly attest that the spring suburban sacrifice is eight li.
translations.idiomatic: 」 All these authorities clearly attest that the spring suburban altar lies eight li away.

sentences.zh: 《孟夏令》云：「其數七。

translations.literal: 」 This is further clear proof of the southern suburb at seven li.
translations.idiomatic: 」 This is further clear evidence that the southern suburban altar lies seven li away.

translations.idiomatic: The 《Central Ordinance》 states: 「Its number is five.

sentences.zh: 」盧植云：「中郊，五里之郊也，」賈逵云：「中兆黃帝之位，並南郊之季，故云兆五帝於四郊也。

translations.literal: 」 Lu Zhi says: 「The central suburb is the five-li suburb,」 Jia Kui says: 「The central altar is the position of the Yellow Emperor, together with the end of the southern suburb, hence it says enshrine the Five Emperors in the four suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Lu Zhi writes: 「The central suburban altar is the five-li suburban altar,」 and Jia Kui writes: 「The central altar marks the position of the Yellow Emperor, combined with the southern suburban season, hence the saying that the Five Emperors are enshrined in the four suburbs.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「中郊，西南未地，去都城五里。

translations.literal: 」 Zheng Xuan says: 「The central suburb, in the southwest wei position, is five li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Zheng Xuan writes: 「The central suburban altar lies in the southwest wei position, five li from the capital.

translations.literal: 」 This is further clear proof of the central suburb at five li.
translations.idiomatic: 」 This is further clear evidence that the central suburban altar lies five li away.

translations.idiomatic: The 《First Month of Autumn Ordinance》 states: 「Its number is nine.

translations.idiomatic: 」 It also says: 「Welcome autumn in the western suburb.

translations.idiomatic: 」 Lu Zhi writes: 「The western suburb, nine li.

translations.idiomatic: 」 Jia Kui writes: 「The western suburb belongs to the Metal Emperor Shao Hao, nine li away.

translations.idiomatic: The 《First Month of Winter Ordinance》 states: 「Its number is six.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「迎冬於北郊。

translations.literal: 」 It also says: 「Welcome winter in the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 」 It also says: 「Welcome winter in the northern suburb.

translations.literal: 」 Lu Zhi says: 「The northern suburb is the six-li suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Lu Zhi writes: 「The northern suburb is the six-li suburban altar.

translations.idiomatic: 」 Jia Kui writes: 「The northern suburb belongs to the Water Emperor Zhuan Xu, six li away,」 and Xu Shen writes: 「The northern suburb is the six-li suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 宋氏《含文嘉》注云：「《周禮》：王畿內千里，二十分其一，以為近郊。

translations.literal: The Song clan's annotated 《Hanwen Jia》 says: 「The 《Rites of Zhou》: within the royal domain one thousand li, one twentieth of it serves as the near suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Song dynasty annotated 《Hanwen Jia》 states: 「The 《Rites of Zhou》 says that within the royal domain of one thousand li, one twentieth constitutes the near suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 近郊五十里，倍之為遠郊。

translations.literal: The near suburb fifty li; doubled, it becomes the far suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The near suburban altar lay fifty li away; doubled, this became the far suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 迎王氣蓋於近郊。

translations.literal: Welcoming the king's qi is done at the near suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The welcoming of the royal qi took place at the near suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 漢不設王畿，則以其方數為郊處。

translations.literal: Han did not establish a royal domain, and so used the directional numbers as the suburban locations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Han did not establish a royal domain, it used the directional numerological distances to determine the suburban locations.

sentences.zh: 故東郊八里，南郊七里，西郊九里，北郊六里，中郊在西南未地五里。

translations.literal: Hence the eastern suburb eight li, southern suburb seven li, western suburb nine li, northern suburb six li, central suburb in the southwest wei position five li.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the eastern suburban altar at eight li, the southern at seven li, the western at nine li, the northern at six li, and the central in the southwest wei position at five li.

sentences.zh: 」《祭祀志》云：「建武二年正月，初制郊兆于雒陽城南七里，依采元始中故事，北郊在雒陽城北四里。

translations.literal: 」 The 《Treatise on Sacrifices》 says: 「In the first month of the second year of Jianwu, suburban altars were first established at seven li south of Luoyang city, following the precedent of the Yuan-shi era; the northern suburb was four li north of Luoyang city.
translations.idiomatic: 」 The 《Treatise on Sacrifices》 records: 「In the first month of the second year of Jianwu, suburban altars were first established seven li south of Luoyang, following the Yuan-shi precedent; the northern suburban altar was four li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」此又漢世南、北郊之明據也。

translations.literal: 」 This is further clear proof of the Han dynasty's southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: 」 This provides further clear evidence for the Han dynasty's southern and northern suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 今地祗准此。

translations.literal: Now the Earth Spirit should follow this standard.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of the Earth Spirit should now follow this standard.

sentences.zh: 至如三十里郊，進乖鄭玄所引殷、周二代之據，退違漢、魏所行故事。

translations.literal: As for a thirty-li suburb, going forward it deviates from the grounds Zheng Xuan cites for the Yin and Zhou two dynasties; going back it violates the precedents followed by Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: A thirty-li suburban distance would violate both the evidence Zheng Xuan cites from the Yin and Zhou dynasties and the precedents followed under Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 凡邑外曰郊。

translations.literal: In general, outside the city is called suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In general, the area outside the city walls is called the suburban zone.

sentences.zh: 今計四郊各以郭門為限，里數依上。

translations.literal: Now calculating the four suburbs, each takes the outer gate as its limit; the number of li follows the above.
