translations.idiomatic: For the four suburban altars, each should be measured from the outer city gate, with the distances given above.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：朝拜日月皆於東西門外。

translations.literal: The 《Rites》: court worship of the sun and moon is all at the outer east and west gates.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites》 stipulate that court worship of the sun and moon takes place outside the eastern and western gates.

sentences.zh: 今日月之位，去城東西，路各三十，竊又未審。

translations.literal: Now the positions of the sun and moon, from the city east and west, each road thirty li -- I privately am again not clear.
translations.idiomatic: The current locations for the sun and moon sacrifices lie thirty li from the city on the east and west roads respectively, which I also find questionable.

sentences.zh: 《禮》又云：「祭日於壇，祭月於坎。

translations.literal: The 《Rites》 also say: 「Sacrifice to the sun at an altar, sacrifice to the moon in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites》 also state: 「Sacrifice to the sun at a raised altar, and to the moon in a sunken pit.

sentences.zh: 」今計造如上。

translations.literal: 」 Now the planned construction is as above.
translations.idiomatic: 」 The current planned construction follows the arrangement described above.

sentences.zh: 《禮儀志》云：「立高禖祠于城南。

translations.literal: The 《Treatise on Ritual》 says: 「Establish the Gaomei shrine south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Treatise on Ritual》 records: 「Establish the Gaomei shrine south of the city.

sentences.zh: 」不雲里數，故今用舊。

translations.literal: 」 It does not give the number of li, and so the present arrangement follows the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: 」 As it does not specify a distance in li, the present practice follows the old arrangement.

sentences.zh: 靈星本非禮事，兆自漢初，專為祈田，恆隸郡縣。

translations.literal: The Spirit Star was originally not a rite of the classics; the altar arose from early Han, devoted solely to praying for harvest, and was constantly subordinate to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Worship of the Spirit Star was never part of classical ritual; the altar originated in early Han specifically to pray for good harvests and had always been administered by commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 《郊祀志》云：「高祖五年，制詔御史，其令天下立靈星祠，牲用太牢，縣邑令、長侍祠。

translations.literal: The 《Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices》 says: 「In the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu, an edict was issued to the Censor, ordering the empire to establish Spirit Star shrines, using the grand sacrificial beast, with district and county magistrates attending the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices》 records: 「In the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu, an edict was issued to the Censor ordering the whole empire to establish Spirit Star shrines, using the grand sacrificial victim, with district and county magistrates presiding at the rites.

sentences.zh: 」晉《祠令》云：「郡、縣、國祠社稷、先農，縣又祠靈星。

translations.literal: 」 The Jin 《Regulations on Shrines》 say: 「Commanderies, counties, and kingdoms sacrifice to the Soil and Grain and the First Farmer; counties also sacrifice to the Spirit Star.
translations.idiomatic: 」 The Jin 《Regulations on Shrines》 state: 「Commanderies, counties, and kingdoms maintain shrines to the Soil and Grain and the First Farmer; counties also maintain shrines to the Spirit Star.

sentences.zh: 」此靈星在天下諸縣之明據也。

translations.literal: 」 This is clear proof that the Spirit Star is in the counties throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: 」 This provides clear evidence that Spirit Star shrines belonged to counties throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 周公廟所以別在洛陽者，蓋緣姬旦創成洛邑，故傳世洛陽，崇祠不絕，以彰厥庸。

translations.literal: The reason the shrine to the Duke of Zhou is separately in Luoyang is probably because Ji Dan completed the establishment of Luoyang, and so through generations in Luoyang honored worship continued unbroken, to manifest his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou shrine stands separately in Luoyang because the Duke of Zhou, Ji Dan, established that city; worship there has continued through the generations to honor his achievement.

sentences.zh: 夷、齊廟者，亦世為洛陽界內神祠。

translations.literal: The shrines to Yi and Qi are likewise through generations spirit shrines within the borders of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The shrines to Bo Yi and Shu Qi have likewise been local spirit temples within Luoyang's jurisdiction for generations.

sentences.zh: 今並移太常，恐乖其本。

translations.literal: Now transferring them all to the Ministry of Rites -- I fear this goes against their original nature.
translations.idiomatic: Transferring them all to the Ministry of Rites would, I fear, violate their original purpose.

sentences.zh: 正下此類甚眾，皆當部郡縣修理，公私施之禱請。

translations.literal: Correcting this, such cases are very numerous; all ought to be maintained by the commanderies and counties under their jurisdiction, with public and private offerings and prayers.
translations.idiomatic: There are many cases of this kind; all should remain under the maintenance of their respective commanderies and counties, with public and private offerings and prayers.

sentences.zh: 竊惟太常所司，郊廟神祇自有常限，無宜臨時斟酌以意，若遂爾妄營，則不免淫祀。

translations.literal: I privately consider that what the Ministry of Rites administers -- suburban, temple, and spirit deities -- has its own fixed limits; it is not fitting to weigh matters ad hoc according to whim; if one rashly undertakes arbitrary arrangements, one cannot avoid improper sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites oversees suburban, temple, and spirit deities within fixed limits; it is not appropriate to make ad hoc arrangements at will, for rash changes would lead to improper worship.

sentences.zh: 二祠在太常，在洛陽，于國一也，然貴在審本。

translations.literal: The two shrines being under the Ministry of Rites or in Luoyang is, for the state, one and the same; yet what is valued is examining the root.
translations.idiomatic: Whether these two shrines fall under the Ministry of Rites or remain in Luoyang is, for the state, a matter of indifference; what matters is respecting their original character.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸蔽，謬忝今職，考括墳籍，博采群議，既無異端，謂粗可依據。

translations.literal: Your subject, being mediocre and obscure, wrongly holds the present office; examining and embracing tomb records, broadly gathering collective opinions, there being no divergent views, I consider it roughly reliable as grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Though mediocre and unworthy of my present office, I have examined ancient records and gathered widely differing opinions; finding no serious dissent, I believe the evidence presented here is sufficient grounds for action.

sentences.zh: 今玄冬務隙，野罄人閑，遷易郊壇，二三為便。

translations.literal: Now in deep winter there is a lull in affairs; the wilds are empty and the people at leisure; to move and change the suburban altars, two or three would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Deep winter brings a lull in affairs, when fields lie idle and people are free; it would be convenient to relocate the suburban altars within two or three months.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「所上乃有明據，但先朝置立已久，且可從舊。」

translations.literal: An edict said: 「What you have submitted indeed has clear grounds, but the former court's establishments have long stood; for now follow the old arrangement.」
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: 「Your memorial presents clear evidence, but the former court's arrangements have stood for many years; for now, let the old practice remain.」

sentences.zh: 先是，孝文於代都，詔中書監高閭、太常少卿陸琇並公孫崇等十餘人，修理金石及八音之器。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Xiaowen at the capital in Dai issued an edict to Director of the Secretariat Gao Lu, Vice Minister of Rites Lu Xiu, together with Gongsun Chong and more than ten others, to repair metal and stone and the eight kinds of instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, while at the capital in Dai, Emperor Xiaowen ordered Director of the Secretariat Gao Lu, Vice Minister of Rites Lu Xiu, Gongsun Chong, and more than ten others to restore metal and stone instruments and the full range of musical instruments.

sentences.zh: 後崇為太樂令，乃上請尚書僕射高肇，更共營理。

translations.literal: Later Chong became Director of Grand Music and submitted a request to Deputy Director of the Department of State Affairs Gao Zhao to undertake joint management anew.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Chong became Director of Grand Music, he petitioned Deputy Director of the Department of State Affairs Gao Zhao to join him in managing the project.

sentences.zh: 宣武詔芳共主之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu ordered Fang to jointly preside over it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu ordered Fang to join him in directing the effort.

sentences.zh: 芳表以禮樂事大，不容輒決，自非博延公卿，廣集儒彥，討論得失，研窮是非，無以垂之萬葉，為不朽之式。

translations.literal: Fang submitted a memorial that rites and music are a great matter and cannot be decided rashly; unless one broadly extends invitation to dukes and ministers, widely gathers Confucian worthies, discusses gains and losses, and exhaustively investigates right and wrong, there is no way to hand it down through ten thousand generations as an immortal model.
translations.idiomatic: Fang submitted a memorial arguing that rites and music are matters of great weight and cannot be decided hastily; only by broadly convening dukes and ministers, gathering Confucian scholars of distinction, debating merits and flaws, and thoroughly investigating right and wrong could a model be established to endure through the ages.

sentences.zh: 被報聽許，數旬之間，頻煩三議。

translations.literal: Receiving a reply granting permission, within several tens of days there were three deliberations in rapid succession.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted, and within several weeks three successive deliberations were convened.

sentences.zh: 於是朝士頗以崇專綜既久，不應乖謬，各默然無發論者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court gentlemen largely considered that Chong had long been in exclusive charge of the whole and ought not to be mistaken, and each remained silent with no one offering arguments.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials largely assumed that Chong, having long supervised the project, could not be in error, and each remained silent, offering no objections.

sentences.zh: 芳乃探引經誥，搜括舊文，共相難質，皆有明據，以為盈縮有差，不合典式。

translations.literal: Fang then searched out and cited canonical texts and edicts, gathered old writings, and they mutually challenged and questioned one another; each had clear evidence, holding that surplus and deficit were inconsistent and did not conform to the canonical model.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then searched through canonical texts and edicts, gathered old writings, and they cross-examined one another. Each side had clear evidence, arguing that the discrepancies in surplus and deficit did not conform to the canonical standard.

sentences.zh: 崇雖示相酬答，而不會問意，卒無以自通。

translations.literal: Although Chong showed responses in kind, he did not grasp the meaning of the questions, and in the end had no way to vindicate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chong offered replies in turn, but failed to grasp the point of the questions and ultimately could not clear himself.

sentences.zh: 尚書依事述奏，仍詔委芳別更考制。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Secretariat presented a report according to the facts, and the emperor further ordered that Fang be entrusted to separately re-examine and establish the system.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Secretariat reported the matter as it stood, and the emperor further ordered Fang to re-examine the system on his own.

sentences.zh: 於是學者彌歸宗焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars increasingly rallied to his school of thought.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter scholars increasingly looked to him as their authority.

sentences.zh: 芳以社稷無樹，又上疏曰：

translations.literal: Fang, noting that the altars of state and grain had no trees, submitted another memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Noting that the altars of state and grain had no trees, Fang submitted another memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 依《合朔儀》注：日有變，以硃絲為繩，以繞系社樹三匝。

translations.literal: According to the commentary on the Rite for the New Moon: when the sun had an anomaly, vermillion silk was made into a cord and wrapped three times around the tree at the altar of the soil god.
translations.idiomatic: According to the commentary on the Rite for the New Moon, when the sun showed an anomaly, a cord of vermillion silk was made and wound three times around the tree at the altar of the soil god.

sentences.zh: 而今無樹。

translations.literal: Yet now there are no trees.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now there are no trees.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮大司徒》職云：「設其社稷之壝而樹之田主，各以其社所宜木。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the duties in the Grand Minister of Education chapter of the Rites of Zhou state: "Establish the earthen mounds for the altars of state and grain and plant trees there as lords of the fields, each according to the wood suited to that altar."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the duties of the Grand Minister of Education in the Rites of Zhou state: "Establish the earthen mounds for the altars of state and grain and plant trees there as lords of the fields, each according to the wood suited to that altar."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「所宜木，謂若松、柏、栗也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "The wood suited to each refers to such trees as pine, cypress, and chestnut."
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "The wood suited to each refers to trees such as pine, cypress, and chestnut."

sentences.zh: 」此其一證也。

translations.literal: " This is the first piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: " This is the first piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 又《小司徒·封人》職云：「掌設王之社壝，為畿封而樹之。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the duties of the Lesser Minister of Education and the Boundary Master state: "They are in charge of establishing the king's altar mound and planting trees to mark the boundaries of the royal domain."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the duties of the Lesser Minister of Education and the Boundary Master state: "They are in charge of establishing the king's altar mound and planting trees to mark the boundaries of the royal domain."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「不言稷者，王主於社；

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "It does not mention the altar of grain because the king's primary altar is that of the soil god;
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "It does not mention the altar of grain because the king's primary concern is the altar of the soil god;

sentences.zh: 稷，社之細也。

translations.literal: the altar of grain is subsidiary to the altar of the soil god."
translations.idiomatic: the altar of grain is subsidiary to the altar of the soil god."

sentences.zh: 」此其二證也。

translations.literal: " This is the second piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: " This is the second piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 又《論語》曰：「哀公問社於宰我。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Analects says: "Duke Ai of Lu asked Zai Wo about the altar of the soil god.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Analects says: "Duke Ai of Lu asked Zai Wo about the altar of the soil god.

sentences.zh: 宰我對曰：夏後氏以松，殷人以柏，周人以栗。

translations.literal: Zai Wo replied: The Xia used pine, the Yin used cypress, the Zhou used chestnut."
translations.idiomatic: Zai Wo replied: The Xia used pine, the Yin used cypress, and the Zhou used chestnut."

sentences.zh: 」是乃土地之所宜也。

translations.literal: " These were the trees suited to the land.
translations.idiomatic: " These were the trees suited to the land.

sentences.zh: 此其三證也。

translations.literal: This is the third piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 又《白武通》：社、稷所以有樹，何也？

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Baihu Tong asks: Why do the altars of state and grain have trees?
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Baihu Tong asks: Why do the altars of state and grain have trees?

sentences.zh: 尊而識之也。

translations.literal: To show reverence and mark them for recognition.
translations.idiomatic: To show reverence and make them recognizable.

sentences.zh: 使人望見既敬之，又所以表功也。

translations.literal: So that when people saw them they would revere them, and also to display their merit.
translations.idiomatic: So that when people saw them they would revere them, and also to display their merit.

sentences.zh: 」案此正解所以有樹之義，了不論有之與無也。

translations.literal: " This explanation precisely clarifies the meaning of having trees—it never discusses whether they exist or not.
translations.idiomatic: " This explanation precisely clarifies the meaning of having trees and never discusses whether they exist or not.

sentences.zh: 此其四證也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 此云「社、稷所以有樹何」，然則稷亦有樹明矣。

translations.literal: This passage asks "Why do the altars of state and grain have trees?"—thus it is clear that the altar of grain also has trees.
translations.idiomatic: This passage asks "Why do the altars of state and grain have trees?"—thus it is clear that the altar of grain also has trees.

sentences.zh: 又《五經通義》云：「天子太社、王社，諸侯國社、侯社，制度奈何？

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Tongyi of the Five Classics states: "The Grand Altar of State and the King's Altar for the Son of Heaven, the State Altar and the Marquis's Altar for feudal lords—what are their regulations?
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Tongyi of the Five Classics states: "The Grand Altar of State and the King's Altar for the Son of Heaven, the State Altar and the Marquis's Altar for feudal lords—what are their regulations?

sentences.zh: 曰，社皆有垣無屋，樹其中以木。

translations.literal: The answer: all altars have walls but no buildings, and trees are planted within them.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: all altars have walls but no buildings, and trees are planted within them.

sentences.zh: 有木者，土主生萬物，萬物莫善於木，故樹木也。

translations.literal: The reason for having trees is that the lord of the soil produces the myriad things, and among the myriad things nothing is better than wood—therefore trees are planted.
translations.idiomatic: The reason for having trees is that the lord of the soil produces the myriad things, and among the myriad things nothing excels wood—therefore trees are planted.

sentences.zh: 」此其五證也，此最其丁甯備解有樹之意也。

translations.literal: " This is the fifth piece of evidence, and it most clearly and completely explains the meaning of having trees.
translations.idiomatic: " This is the fifth piece of evidence, and it most clearly and completely explains the meaning of having trees.

sentences.zh: 又《五經要義》云：「社必樹之以木。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Yaoyi of the Five Classics states: "The altar of the soil god must be planted with trees.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Yaoyi of the Five Classics states: "The altar of the soil god must be planted with trees.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·司徒》職曰：班社而樹之，各以土地所生。

translations.literal: The duties of the Minister of Education in the Rites of Zhou say: Altars are distributed and trees planted, each according to what the land produces.
translations.idiomatic: The duties of the Minister of Education in the Rites of Zhou say: Altars are distributed and trees planted, each according to what the land produces.

sentences.zh: 《尚書·逸篇》曰：太社惟松，東社惟柏，南社惟梓，西社惟栗，北社惟槐。

translations.literal: The apocryphal chapter of the Documents says: The Grand Altar uses only pine, the Eastern Altar only cypress, the Southern Altar only catalpa, the Western Altar only chestnut, the Northern Altar only locust."
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal chapter of the Documents says: The Grand Altar uses only pine, the Eastern Altar only cypress, the Southern Altar only catalpa, the Western Altar only chestnut, and the Northern Altar only locust."

sentences.zh: 」此其六證也。

translations.literal: " This is the sixth piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: " This is the sixth piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 此又太社及四方皆有樹別之明據也。

translations.literal: This is further clear evidence that the Grand Altar and the altars of the four directions each have distinct trees.
translations.idiomatic: This is further clear evidence that the Grand Altar and the altars of the four directions each have distinct trees.

sentences.zh: 又見諸家《禮圖》，社稷圖皆畫為樹，唯誡社、誡稷無樹。

translations.literal: Furthermore, in the ritual diagrams of various schools, the altars of state and grain are all depicted as trees—only the warning altars of state and grain have no trees.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in the ritual diagrams of various schools, the altars of state and grain are all depicted with trees—only the warning altars of state and grain have none.

sentences.zh: 此其七證也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 雖辨有樹之據，猶未正所植之木。

translations.literal: Although the evidence for having trees had been established, the species of tree to be planted had not yet been determined.
translations.idiomatic: Although the evidence for planting trees had been established, the species to be planted had not yet been determined.

sentences.zh: 案《論語》稱「夏後氏以松，殷人以柏，周人以栗」，便是世代不同。

translations.literal: The Analects says "the Xia used pine, the Yin used cypress, the Zhou used chestnut"—this indicates that different dynasties used different trees.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says "the Xia used pine, the Yin used cypress, the Zhou used chestnut"—this shows that different dynasties used different trees.

sentences.zh: 而《尚書·逸篇》則云「太社惟松」，如此，便以一代之中而立社各異也。

translations.literal: But the apocryphal chapter of the Documents says "the Grand Altar uses only pine"—in that case, within a single dynasty different altars would use different trees.
translations.idiomatic: But the apocryphal chapter of the Documents says "the Grand Altar uses only pine"—which would mean that within a single dynasty different altars would use different trees.

sentences.zh: 愚以為宜植以松。

translations.literal: I humbly believe pine should be planted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe pine should be planted.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: On what grounds?
translations.idiomatic: On what grounds?

sentences.zh: 《逸書》云「太社惟松」，今者植松，不慮失禮。

translations.literal: The apocryphal Documents say "the Grand Altar uses only pine." To plant pine now would not risk breach of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal Documents say "the Grand Altar uses only pine." To plant pine now would not risk any breach of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 惟稷無成證。

translations.literal: Only the altar of grain lacks conclusive evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Only the altar of grain lacks conclusive evidence.

sentences.zh: 稷乃社之細，蓋亦不離松也。

translations.literal: The altar of grain is subsidiary to the altar of the soil god, and presumably would also not depart from pine.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of grain is subsidiary to the altar of the soil god and presumably would not depart from pine either.

sentences.zh: 宣武從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 芳沈雅方正，概尚甚高，《經》、《傳》多通，孝文尤器敬之，動相顧訪。

translations.literal: Fang was deep, refined, upright, and square in character, with elevated principles. He was broadly versed in the Classics and their commentaries. Emperor Xiaowen especially valued and esteemed him, frequently consulting him on matters.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was deep, refined, upright, and principled, with elevated standards. He was broadly versed in the Classics and their commentaries. Emperor Xiaowen especially valued and respected him, consulting him frequently on important matters.

sentences.zh: 太子恂之在東宮，孝文欲為納芳女，芳辭以年貌非宜，帝歎其謙慎。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Xun was in the Eastern Palace, Emperor Xiaowen wished to marry Fang's daughter to him. Fang declined, citing unsuitable age and appearance. The emperor sighed at his modest prudence.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun was in the Eastern Palace, Emperor Xiaowen wished to marry Fang's daughter to him. Fang declined on grounds of unsuitable age and appearance, and the emperor sighed at his modest prudence.

sentences.zh: 帝更敕芳舉其宗女，芳乃稱其族子長文之女，孝文乃為恂娉之，與鄭懿女對為左右孺子焉。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Fang to recommend a clanswoman. Fang named the daughter of his clansman Chang Wen. Emperor Xiaowen then betrothed her to Xun, and she and Zheng Yi's daughter served together as junior consorts on his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Fang to recommend a clanswoman. Fang named the daughter of his clansman Chang Wen. Emperor Xiaowen betrothed her to Xun, and she and Zheng Yi's daughter served together as junior consorts at the crown prince's left and right.

sentences.zh: 崔光於芳有中表之敬，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Cui Guang held cousinly respect for Fang and on every matter sought and looked up to his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang held cousinly respect for Fang and on every matter sought his counsel and looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 芳撰鄭玄所注《周官·儀禮音》、干寶所注《周官音》、王肅所注《尚書音》、何休所注《公羊音》、范寧所注《穀梁音》、韋昭所注《國語音》、范曄《後漢書音》各一卷，《辯類》三卷，《徐州人地錄》二十卷，《急就篇續注音義證》三卷，《毛詩箋音義證》十卷，《禮記義證》十卷，《周官·儀禮義證》各五卷。

translations.literal: Fang compiled one fascicle each of phonological glosses on the Rites of Zhou and Rites as annotated by Zheng Xuan, on the Rites of Zhou as annotated by Gan Bao, on the Documents as annotated by Wang Su, on the Gongyang Commentary as annotated by He Xiu, on the Guliang Commentary as annotated by Fan Ning, on the Discourses of the States as annotated by Wei Zhao, and on Fan Ye's Book of Later Han; three fascicles of Classificatory Distinctions; twenty fascicles of Record of the People and Land of Xuzhou; three fascicles of Continued Glosses and Evidential Analysis of the Rapid Composition Primer; ten fascicles of Glosses and Evidential Analysis of Mao's Commentary on the Odes and Evidential Analysis of the Record of Rites; and five fascicles each of Evidential Analysis of the Rites of Zhou and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fang compiled one fascicle each of phonological glosses on the Rites of Zhou and Rites as annotated by Zheng Xuan, on the Rites of Zhou as annotated by Gan Bao, on the Documents as annotated by Wang Su, on the Gongyang Commentary as annotated by He Xiu, on the Guliang Commentary as annotated by Fan Ning, on the Discourses of the States as annotated by Wei Zhao, and on Fan Ye's Book of Later Han; three fascicles of Classificatory Distinctions; twenty fascicles of Record of the People and Land of Xuzhou; three fascicles of Continued Glosses and Evidential Analysis of the Rapid Composition Primer; ten fascicles each of Glosses and Evidential Analysis of Mao's Commentary on the Odes and Evidential Analysis of the Record of Rites; and five fascicles each of Evidential Analysis of the Rites of Zhou and Rites.

sentences.zh: 崔光表求以中書監讓芳，宣武不許。

translations.literal: Cui Guang submitted a memorial asking to yield the post of Director of the Secretariat to Fang. Emperor Xuanwu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang submitted a memorial asking to yield the post of Director of the Secretariat to Fang, but Emperor Xuanwu did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮東將軍、徐州刺史，諡文貞侯。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously awarded the titles General Who Guards the East and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Marquis Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously awarded the titles General Who Guards the East and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Marquis Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 長子懌，字祖欣。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Yi, styled Zuxin.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Yi, styled Zuxin.

sentences.zh: 雅有父風，頗好文翰。

translations.literal: He naturally possessed his father's manner and was quite fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He naturally possessed his father's manner and was quite fond of literary composition.

sentences.zh: 曆徐州別駕、兗州左軍府長史、司空諮議參軍，屢為行台出使，所曆皆有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He served successively as Administrator in Xuzhou, Chief Clerk of the Left Army Office in Yanzhou, and Advisory Aide to the Minister of Works. He was repeatedly dispatched on missions by field headquarters, and in every post earned praise for fitting his office.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Administrator in Xuzhou, Chief Clerk of the Left Army Office in Yanzhou, and Advisory Aide to the Minister of Works. He was repeatedly dispatched on missions by field headquarters, and in every post earned praise for fulfilling his duties well.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎常侍、徐州大中正，行郢州事，尋遷安南將軍、大司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Fast Carriage and Grand Arbiter of Xuzhou, and held concurrent charge of Yingzhou affairs. Soon after he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Fast Carriage and Grand Arbiter of Xuzhou, and held concurrent charge of Yingzhou affairs. Soon after he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈徐州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously named Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Jian.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟廞以第三子峻為後。

translations.literal: He had no sons. His younger brother Yin made his third son Jun the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons. His younger brother Yin made his third son Jun the heir.

sentences.zh: 廞字景興，好學強立。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Jingxing, loved learning and was forceful and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Jingxing, loved learning and was forceful and upright.

sentences.zh: 善事當世，高肇之盛及清河王懌為宰輔，廞皆與其子侄交遊。

translations.literal: He knew how to get along in his age. During Gao Zhao's ascendancy and when Prince of Qinghe Yi served as chief minister, Yin cultivated friendships with their sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to navigate the world of his day. During Gao Zhao's ascendancy and when Prince of Qinghe Yi served as chief minister, Yin cultivated friendships with their sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，又與太后兄子往還相好。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling presided over the court, he also associated on friendly terms with the empress dowager's brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling presided over the court, he also maintained friendly relations with the empress dowager's brother's son.

sentences.zh: 太后令廞以詩武授弟元吉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered Yin to teach his younger brother Yuanji literary and martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered Yin to instruct his younger brother Yuanji in literary and martial arts.

sentences.zh: 稍遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，除散騎常侍，遷驃騎大將軍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry, then promoted to General of Rapid Cavalry and Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry, then promoted to General of Rapid Cavalry and Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 孝武于顯陽殿講《孝經》，廞為執經，雖酬答論難未能精盡，而風采音制，足有可觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Manifest Yang. Yin served as the scripture-holder. Although his responses and debate did not reach full depth, his bearing, voice, and demeanor were quite worth watching.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Manifest Yang. Yin served as the scripture-holder. Although his responses and debate lacked full depth, his bearing, voice, and presence were quite impressive.

sentences.zh: 尋兼都官尚書，又兼殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he held concurrent posts as Minister of Justice and Minister of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held concurrent posts as Minister of Justice and Minister of Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及孝武入關，齊神武至洛，責廞誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass, Qi Shenwu arrived at Luoyang and had Yin condemned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass, Gao Huan arrived at Luoyang and had Yin condemned and executed.

sentences.zh: 子騭，字子升。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, styled Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhi, styled Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 少有風氣，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirited character and was fairly versed in literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had a spirited character and was fairly versed in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 位徐州開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attendant Gentleman in the staff of the Xuzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Xuzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 父廞之死，騭率勒鄉部赴兗州，與刺史樊子鵠抗禦王師。

translations.literal: After his father Yin's death, Zhi led local militias to Yanzhou and, together with Governor Fan Zihuo, resisted the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: After his father Yin's death, Zhi led local militias to Yanzhou and, together with Governor Fan Zihuo, resisted the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 每戰，流涕突陣。

translations.literal: In every battle he wept as he charged the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he wept as he charged the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 城陷，禽送晉陽。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he was captured and sent to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he was captured and sent to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 齊神武矜而赦之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan took pity on him and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan took pity on him and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 文襄為儀同開府，以騭為屬本州大中正，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang served as a general of combined regiments with his own field headquarters, he made Zhi a subordinate and Grand Arbiter of his native province. Zhi then became a Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng served as honorary commander with his own field headquarters, he made Zhi a subordinate and Grand Arbiter of his native province. Zhi then became a Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 時與梁和通，騭前後受敕對其使一十六人。

translations.literal: At the time peace had been established with Liang. Zhi received orders on sixteen separate occasions to receive and respond to their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: At the time peace had been established with Liang. Zhi received orders on sixteen separate occasions to receive and respond to their envoys.

sentences.zh: 為司徒左長史，卒，贈南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Education. When he died, he was posthumously named Governor of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Education. When he died, he was posthumously named Governor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 廞弟彧，位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Yu held the post of Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with the Golden Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Yu held the post of Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with the Golden Girdle.

sentences.zh: 彧子逖。

translations.literal: Yu had a son Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a son Ti.

sentences.zh: 逖字子長，少聰敏。

translations.literal: Ti, styled Zichang, was clever and quick from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Ti, styled Zichang, was clever and quick from youth.

sentences.zh: 好弋獵騎射，以行樂為事；

translations.literal: He loved falconry, hunting, and mounted archery, and made going out for pleasure his occupation;
translations.idiomatic: He loved falconry, hunting, and mounted archery, and made going out for pleasure his occupation;

sentences.zh: 愛交遊，善戲謔。

translations.literal: He loved making friends and was skilled at jesting banter.
translations.idiomatic: He loved making friends and was skilled at jesting banter.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄以為永安公浚開府行參軍。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Wenxiang appointed him Acting Aide in the field headquarters of Prince Yong'an Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng appointed him Acting Aide in the field headquarters of Prince Yong'an Jun.

sentences.zh: 逖遠離家鄉，倦於羈旅，發憤自勵，專精讀書。

translations.literal: Ti, far from home and weary of life as a traveler, stirred himself to diligence and devoted himself exclusively to reading.
translations.idiomatic: Far from home and weary of life on the road, Ti stirred himself to diligence and devoted himself exclusively to reading.

sentences.zh: 晉陽都會之所，霸朝人士攸集，咸務於宴集。

translations.literal: Jinyang was a great gathering place where officials of the hegemonic court assembled, all devoted to banquets and gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang was a great gathering place where officials of the hegemonic court assembled, all devoted to feasting and conviviality.

sentences.zh: 逖在遊宴之中，卷不離手，遇有文籍所未見者，則終日諷誦，或通夜不歸。

translations.literal: Even amid outings and feasts, Ti never let his scroll leave his hand. When he encountered texts he had not seen before, he would recite them all day, sometimes not returning home all night.
translations.idiomatic: Even amid outings and feasts, Ti never let his scroll leave his hand. When he encountered texts he had not seen before, he would recite them all day, sometimes not returning home until dawn.

sentences.zh: 其好學如此。

translations.literal: Such was his love of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his love of learning.

sentences.zh: 亦留心文藻，頗工詩詠。

translations.literal: He also cultivated literary grace and was quite skilled at composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He also cultivated literary grace and was quite skilled at composing poetry.

sentences.zh: 武成時，和士開寵要，逖附之。

translations.literal: During the reign of Wucheng, He Shikai was favored and influential, and Ti attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Wucheng, He Shikai was favored and influential, and Ti attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 正授中書侍郎，入典機密。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and entered into handling state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and entered into handling state secrets.

sentences.zh: 時李愔獻賦，言天保中被讒。

translations.literal: At the time Li Yin submitted a rhapsody that spoke of having been slandered during the Tianbao reign.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Yin submitted a rhapsody that spoke of having been slandered during the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 逖摘其文，奏曰：「誹謗先朝，大不敬。

translations.literal: Ti extracted passages from the text and memorialized: "This slanders the former reign—a grave offense of disrespect."
translations.idiomatic: Ti extracted passages from the text and memorialized: "This slanders the former reign—a grave offense of disrespect."

sentences.zh: 」武成怒，大加鞭樸。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wucheng was enraged and had Li Yin severely flogged with the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wucheng was enraged and had Li Yin severely flogged.

sentences.zh: 逖喜復前憾，曰：「高捶兩下，執鞭一百，何如呼劉二時。

translations.literal: Ti, delighted to settle an old grudge, said: "Two blows from the high cudgel and a hundred strokes with the whip—how does that compare to when they summoned Liu the Second?"
translations.idiomatic: Ti, delighted to settle an old score, said: "Two blows from the high cudgel and a hundred strokes with the whip—how does that compare to when they summoned Liu the Second?"

sentences.zh: 」尋兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he held the concurrent post of Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry and served as chief envoy on a mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he held the concurrent post of Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry and served as chief envoy on a mission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 逖欲獨擅文藻，不願與文士同行。

translations.literal: Ti wanted to monopolize literary display and did not wish to travel with literary men.
translations.idiomatic: Ti wanted to monopolize literary display and did not wish to travel with literary men.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎王松年妹夫盧士游，性沈密，逖求以為副。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Shiyou, son-in-law of Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Wang Songnian, was deep and discreet in character, and Ti requested him as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lu Shiyou, son-in-law of Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Wang Songnian, was deep and discreet in character, and Ti requested him as deputy.

sentences.zh: 又逖姊魏家者，收時已放出，逖因次欲嫁之士遊，不許。

translations.literal: Also, Ti's elder sister, who had married into the Wei family, had already been released during Wei Shou's time. Ti then wished to marry her off next to Shiyou, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Also, Ti's elder sister, who had married into the Wei family, had already been released during Wei Shou's time. Ti then wished to marry her off to Shiyou next, but permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 逖恐事露，亦不逼焉。

translations.literal: Ti, fearing the matter would be exposed, did not press it.
translations.idiomatic: Ti, fearing the matter would be exposed, did not press it.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor within the Yellow Gate and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervisor within the Yellow Gate and compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，除假儀同三司，聘周使副。

translations.literal: He was further given the concurrent post of Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry, appointed Acting Honorary Commander-in-Chief of Three Armies, and served as deputy envoy on a mission to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given the concurrent post of Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry, appointed Acting Honorary Commander-in-Chief of Three Armies, and served as deputy envoy on a mission to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 二國始通，禮儀未定，逖與周朝議論往復，斟酌古今，事多合禮，兼文辭可觀，甚行名譽。

translations.literal: When the two states first established relations, ceremonial protocol had not yet been fixed. Ti exchanged arguments back and forth with the Zhou court, weighing ancient and modern practice. Most matters accorded with ritual propriety, and his literary style was also notable. He gained considerable renown.
translations.idiomatic: When the two states first opened diplomatic relations, ceremonial protocol had not yet been settled. Ti debated back and forth with the Zhou court, weighing ancient and modern practice. Most of his positions accorded with ritual propriety, and his prose was impressive as well. He won considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: After returning from the mission, he was appointed Honorary Commander-in-Chief of Three Armies.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the mission, he was appointed Honorary Commander-in-Chief of Three Armies.

sentences.zh: 及武成崩，和士開欲改元，議者各異。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died, He Shikai wished to change the reign title, but those who deliberated differed in opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng died, He Shikai wished to change the reign title, but the deliberators could not agree.

sentences.zh: 逖請為「武平」，私謂士開曰：「武平反為明輔，逖作此以為公。

translations.literal: Ti proposed "Wuping," privately telling He Shikai: "Reversed, Wuping becomes Pingwu, which sounds like 'ministry aid'--I propose this for your sake."
translations.idiomatic: Ti proposed "Wuping," privately telling He Shikai: "Reversed, Wuping becomes Pingwu, which sounds like 'ministry aid'--I propose this for your sake."

sentences.zh: 」士開悅而從之。

translations.literal: " He Shikai was pleased and followed his suggestion.
translations.idiomatic: " He Shikai was pleased and followed his suggestion.

sentences.zh: 時士開為眾口所排，婁定遠同輔政，逖遂回附之，使得西貨，悉以餉定遠。

translations.literal: At the time He Shikai was being pushed aside by public opinion, and Lou Dingyuan shared in the regency. Ti then turned to attach himself to Lou, obtaining Western goods and sending them all to Dingyuan as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time He Shikai was being pushed aside by public opinion, and Lou Dingyuan shared in the regency. Ti then switched allegiance to Lou, obtaining Western goods and sending them all to Dingyuan as gifts.

sentences.zh: 定遠外任，逖不自安，又陰結斛律明月、胡長仁以自固。

translations.literal: When Dingyuan took an outside appointment, Ti felt insecure and secretly cultivated ties with Hulu Mingyue and Hu Changren to strengthen his position.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingyuan took an outside appointment, Ti felt insecure and secretly cultivated ties with Hulu Mingyue and Hu Changren to shore up his position.

sentences.zh: 士開知之，未甚信，忽于明月門巷逢之，彌以為實。

translations.literal: He Shikai learned of this but did not fully believe it until, by chance, he encountered Ti in Mingyue's lane--and then believed it all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai learned of this but did not fully believe it until, by chance, he ran into Ti in Mingyue's lane--and then took it as confirmed.

sentences.zh: 初，逖名宦未達時，欲事祖珽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ti had not yet attained fame and office, he wished to serve Zu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Ti had attained fame and office, he wished to serve Zu Ting.

sentences.zh: 珽未原，謂人曰：「我言彭城楚子，應有氣俠，唯將崔季舒詩示人，殊乖氣望。

translations.literal: Zu Ting did not forgive him and said to others: "I speak of the Chu lad from Pengcheng--he ought to have spirit and chivalry--yet all he does is show people Cui Jishu's poems. That falls far short of what one expects of his character."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting did not forgive him and said to others: "I speak of the Chu lad from Pengcheng--he ought to have spirit and chivalry--yet all he does is show people Cui Jishu's poems. That falls far short of what one expects of him."

sentences.zh: 」逖乃為弟娶珽女，遂成密好。

translations.literal: " Ti then had his younger brother marry Zu's daughter, and they formed a close alliance.
translations.idiomatic: " Ti then had his younger brother marry Zu's daughter, and they formed a close alliance.

sentences.zh: 珽之將訴趙彥深、和士開也，先與逖謀，逖乃告二人。

translations.literal: When Zu Ting was about to bring grievances against Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai, he first plotted with Ti--but Ti then informed the two men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ting was about to bring grievances against Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai, he first plotted with Ti--but Ti then informed the two men.

sentences.zh: 故二人得為之計。

translations.literal: Thus the two men were able to prepare countermeasures.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the two men were able to prepare countermeasures.

sentences.zh: 珽被黜，令弟出其妻。

translations.literal: Zu Ting was dismissed and made Ti's brother divorce his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting was dismissed and made Ti's brother divorce his wife.

sentences.zh: 及是，逖解士開所嫌。

translations.literal: On this occasion, Ti cleared away He Shikai's suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, Ti cleared away He Shikai's suspicions.

sentences.zh: 尋出為仁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was sent out as Governor of Renzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was sent out as Governor of Renzhou.

sentences.zh: 珽乃要行台尚書盧潛陷逖，許潛重遷。

translations.literal: Zu Ting then tried to get Mobile Secretariat Minister Lu Qian to frame Ti, promising Lu a major transfer in return.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting then tried to get Mobile Secretariat Minister Lu Qian to frame Ti, promising Lu a major transfer in return.

sentences.zh: 潛曰：「如此事，吾不為也。

translations.literal: Lu Qian said: "I will not do such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian said: "I will not do such a thing."

sentences.zh: 」更戒逖而護之。

translations.literal: " Instead he warned Ti and protected him.
translations.idiomatic: " Instead he warned Ti and protected him.

sentences.zh: 後被征還，待詔文林館，重除散騎常侍，奏門下事。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled, kept at the Hall of Literary Groves awaiting imperial orders, reappointed Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry, and reported affairs to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled, kept at the Hall of Literary Groves awaiting imperial orders, reappointed Regular Attendant of the Scatterbrushing Cavalry, and reported affairs to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾與崔季舒等同戮，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed together with Cui Jishu and others. He was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed together with Cui Jishu and others, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 所制文筆三十卷。

translations.literal: The collected writings he produced ran to thirty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: The collected writings he produced ran to thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子逸人，開府行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yiren served as Acting Aide in a field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiren served as Acting Aide in a field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，終於洛陽令。

translations.literal: He served under the Sui and ended his career as Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served under the Sui and ended his career as Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 芳懋從子懋。

translations.literal: Fang Mao had a younger clansman Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Mao had a younger clansman Mao.

sentences.zh: 懋字仲華，祖泰之，父承伯，仕宋並有名位。

translations.literal: Mao, styled Zhonghua, had grandfather Taizhi and father Chengbai--all three served in Song and held noted rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, styled Zhonghua, had grandfather Taizhi and father Chengbai--all three served in Song and held noted rank.

sentences.zh: 懋聰敏好學，博綜經史；

translations.literal: Mao was clever, quick to learn, and broadly versed in the classics and histories;
translations.idiomatic: Mao was clever, quick to learn, and broadly versed in the classics and histories;

sentences.zh: 善草隸書，識奇字。

translations.literal: skilled in cursive and clerical script, and versed in unusual characters.
translations.idiomatic: skilled in cursive and clerical script, and versed in unusual characters.

sentences.zh: 宣武初入朝，位尚書外兵郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu first entered court, he held the post of Director in the Outer Troops section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu first entered court, he held the post of Director in the Outer Troops section of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 芳甚重之，凡所撰朝廷軌儀，皆與參量。

translations.literal: Fang greatly valued him, and in all court protocol Fang composed, Mao participated in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Fang greatly valued him, and in all court protocol Fang composed, Mao participated in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書博議，懋與殿中郎袁翻常為議主。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat held broad deliberations, Mao and Palace Attendant Yuan Fan often served as chief debaters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat held broad deliberations, Mao and Palace Attendant Yuan Fan often served as chief debaters.

sentences.zh: 達于從政，台中疑事，咸所訪決。

translations.literal: He was adept at governance, and all doubtful matters at headquarters were referred to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept at governance, and all doubtful matters at headquarters were referred to him for decision.

sentences.zh: 尚書李平與結莫逆交。

translations.literal: He formed with Secretariat Minister Li Ping an inseparable friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He formed with Secretariat Minister Li Ping an inseparable friendship.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉，領郎中，兼東宮中舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers, continued as Director, and concurrently served as Attendant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers, continued as Director, and concurrently served as Attendant in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 轉員外常侍、鎮遠將軍，領考功郎中，立考課之科，明黜陟之法，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: He became Extraordinary Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and continued as Director of Merit Assessment. He established assessment categories and clarified rules for promotion and demotion--very systematic.
translations.idiomatic: He became Extraordinary Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and continued as Director of Merit Assessment. He established assessment categories and clarified rules for promotion and demotion--very systematic.

sentences.zh: 孝昭初，大軍攻硤石，懋為李平行台郎中。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaozhao's reign, when the great army attacked Xiashi, Mao served as Director in Li Ping's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaozhao's reign, when the great army attacked Xiashi, Mao served as Director in Li Ping's field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 城拔，懋頗有功。

translations.literal: When the city was taken, Mao rendered considerable service.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was taken, Mao rendered considerable service.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌愛其風雅，常目而送之曰：「劉生堂堂，搢紳領袖，若天假之年，必為魏朝宰輔。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi admired his elegance and refinement, often watching him depart and saying: "Master Liu is magnificent--a leader among the gentry. If Heaven grants him years, he will surely become a chief minister of the Wei court."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi admired his elegance and refinement, often watching him go and saying: "Master Liu is magnificent--a leader among the gentry. If Heaven grants him years, he will surely become chief minister of the Wei court."

sentences.zh: 」詔懋與諸才學之士撰成儀令。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Mao, together with other men of talent and learning, to compile completed ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Mao, together with other men of talent and learning, to compile completed ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 懌為宰相積年，禮懋尤重，令諸子師之。

translations.literal: Yi served as chief minister for many years and treated Mao with special respect, ordering his sons to take Mao as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served as chief minister for many years and treated Mao with special respect, ordering his sons to take Mao as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Marshal of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Marshal of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 熙平二年冬，暴病卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xiping, he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Xiping, he died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 家甚清貧，亡之日，徙四壁而已。

translations.literal: His household was very poor; at his death there was nothing but bare walls to be moved.
translations.idiomatic: His household was very poor; at his death there was nothing but bare walls to be moved.

sentences.zh: 太傅懌及當時才俊莫不痛惜之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi and all the talented men of the age grieved deeply for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yi and all the talented men of the age grieved deeply for him.

sentences.zh: 贈持節、前將軍、南泰州刺史，諡曰宣簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the insignia of authority, the title Former General, and Governor of Southern Taizhou, with the posthumous epithet Xuan Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the insignia of authority, the title Former General, and Governor of Southern Taizhou, with the posthumous epithet Xuan Jian.

sentences.zh: 懋詩誄賦頌及文筆見稱于時，又撰諸器物造作之始十五卷，名曰《物祖》。

translations.literal: Mao's poems, dirges, rhapsodies, eulogies, and collected writings were acclaimed in their day. He also compiled fifteen fascicles on the origins of various implements and constructions, entitled Origins of Things.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's poems, dirges, rhapsodies, eulogies, and collected writings were acclaimed in their day. He also compiled fifteen fascicles on the origins of various implements and constructions, entitled Origins of Things.

sentences.zh: 常爽，字仕明，河內溫人，魏太常卿林六世孫也。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang, styled Shiming, was a native of Wen in Henei and sixth-generation descendant of Lin, Grand Minister of Ceremonial of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang, styled Shiming, was a native of Wen in Henei and sixth-generation descendant of Lin, Grand Minister of Ceremonial of Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖珍，苻堅南安太守，因世亂，遂居涼州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Nan'an under Fu Jian; because of the turmoil of the times, he settled in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Nan'an under Fu Jian; because of the turmoil of the times, he settled in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父坦，乞伏世鎮遠將軍、大夏鎮將、顯美侯。

translations.literal: His father Tan, under the Qifu regime, was General Who Guards the Distance, Garrison Commander of Daxia, and Marquis of Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan, under the Qifu regime, was General Who Guards the Distance, Garrison Commander of Daxia, and Marquis of Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 爽少而聰敏，嚴正有志概，雖家人僮隸未嘗見其寬誕之容。

translations.literal: Shuang was clever from youth, stern and upright with high aspiration; even household servants and slaves never saw an indulgent or frivolous expression on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was clever from youth, stern and upright with high aspiration; even household servants and slaves never saw an indulgent or frivolous expression on his face.

sentences.zh: 篤志好學，博聞強識，明習緯候、《五經》、百家，多所研綜。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to learning with broad knowledge and strong memory, thoroughly versed in omen lore, the Five Classics, and the hundred schools--he synthesized them extensively.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to learning with broad knowledge and strong memory, thoroughly versed in omen lore, the Five Classics, and the hundred schools--he synthesized them extensively.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮命，皆不就。

translations.literal: He declined all honorary appointments from province and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He declined all honorary appointments from province and commandery.

sentences.zh: 武成西征涼土，爽與兄士國歸款軍門。

translations.literal: When Wucheng marched west against Liang territory, Shuang and his elder brother Shiguo came to offer allegiance at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng marched west against Liang territory, Shuang and his elder brother Shiguo came to offer allegiance at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 武成嘉之，賜士國爵五品，顯美男；

translations.literal: Wucheng commended them, granting Shiguo fifth-rank nobility and the title Baron of Xianmei;
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng commended them, granting Shiguo fifth-rank nobility and the title Baron of Xianmei;

sentences.zh: 爽為六品，拜宣威將軍。

translations.literal: Shuang received sixth rank and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang received sixth rank and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might.

sentences.zh: 是時，戎車屢駕，征伐為事，貴遊子弟未遑學術。

translations.literal: At that time the war chariots rolled out again and again and campaigns were the business at hand; sons of noble families had no leisure for scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the war chariots rolled out again and again and campaigns were the business at hand; sons of noble families had no leisure for scholarship.

sentences.zh: 爽置館溫水之右，教授門徒七百餘人，京師學業，翕然復興。

translations.literal: Shuang established a lodge on the right bank of the Wen River and instructed more than seven hundred disciples. Scholarship in the capital region revived with gathering momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang established a lodge on the right bank of the Wen River and instructed more than seven hundred disciples. Scholarship in the capital region revived with gathering momentum.

sentences.zh: 爽立訓甚有勸罰之科，弟子事之，若嚴君焉。

translations.literal: Shuang established teachings with clear rules of encouragement and punishment; disciples served him as they would a strict father.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang established teachings with clear rules of encouragement and punishment; disciples served him as they would a strict father.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射元贊、平原太守司馬真安、著作郎程靈虯皆是爽教所就。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yuan Zan, Administrator of Pingyuan Sima Zhen'an, and Compiler Cheng Lingqiu were all products of Shuang's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yuan Zan, Administrator of Pingyuan Sima Zhen'an, and Compiler Cheng Lingqiu were all products of Shuang's instruction.

sentences.zh: 崔浩、高允並稱爽之嚴教，獎勵有方。

translations.literal: Cui Hao and Gao Yun both praised Shuang's strict teaching and his well-directed encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao and Gao Yun both praised Shuang's strict teaching and his well-directed encouragement.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「文翁柔勝，先生剛克，立教雖殊，成人一也。

translations.literal: Gao Yun said: "Wen Weng prevailed through gentleness; the Master prevails through firmness. Their methods of instruction differ, yet in forming people they achieve the same end."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun said: "Wen Weng prevailed through gentleness; the Master prevails through firmness. Their methods of instruction differ, yet in forming people they achieve the same end."

sentences.zh: 」其為通識嘆服如此。

translations.literal: " Scholars of broad learning admired him to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: " Scholars of broad learning admired him to this degree.

sentences.zh: 因教授之暇，述《六經略注》，以廣製作，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: In intervals between teaching, he composed Summary Notes on the Six Classics to expand his literary production--very systematic.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals between teaching, he composed Summary Notes on the Six Classics to expand his literary production--very systematic.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface reads:
translations.idiomatic: Its preface reads:

sentences.zh: 《傳》稱立天之道，曰陰與陽；

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to set forth yin and yang;"
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to set forth yin and yang;"

sentences.zh: 立地之道，曰柔與剛；

translations.literal: "To establish the Way of Earth is to set forth softness and firmness;"
translations.idiomatic: "To establish the Way of Earth is to set forth softness and firmness;"

sentences.zh: 立人之道，曰仁與義。

translations.literal: "To establish the Way of Man is to set forth benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: "To establish the Way of Man is to set forth benevolence and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 然則仁義者，人之性也；

translations.literal: Thus benevolence and righteousness are the nature of man;
translations.idiomatic: Thus benevolence and righteousness are the nature of man;

sentences.zh: 經典者，身之文也。

translations.literal: the classics are the ornament of the person.
translations.idiomatic: the classics are the ornament of the person.

sentences.zh: 皆以陶鑄神情，啟悟耳目，未有不由學而能成其器，不由習而能利其業。

translations.literal: Both serve to mold the spirit and awaken the senses. None can complete their capacity without learning, nor can they benefit their work without practice.
translations.idiomatic: Both serve to mold the spirit and awaken the senses. None can complete their capacity without learning, nor can they benefit their work without practice.

sentences.zh: 是故季路勇士也，服道以成忠烈之概；

translations.literal: Thus Zilu was a warrior, yet by embracing the Way he achieved the stature of loyal martyrdom;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zilu was a warrior, yet by embracing the Way he achieved the stature of loyal martyrdom;

sentences.zh: 寧越庸夫也，講藝以全高尚之節。

translations.literal: Ning Yue was a common man, yet by studying the arts he preserved the integrity of high principle.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Yue was a common man, yet by studying the arts he preserved the integrity of high principle.

sentences.zh: 蓋所由者習也，所因者本也；

translations.literal: What one travels by is practice; what one relies on is the root;
translations.idiomatic: What one travels by is practice; what one relies on is the root;

sentences.zh: 本立而道生，身文而德備焉。

translations.literal: when the root is established the Way arises, and when the person is adorned virtue is complete.
translations.idiomatic: when the root is established the Way arises, and when the person is adorned virtue is complete.

sentences.zh: 昔者先王之訓天下也，莫不導以《詩》、《書》，教以《禮》、《樂》，移其風俗，和其人民。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the former kings instructed the realm, none failed to guide it with the Odes and Documents, teach it with the Rites and Music, transform its customs, and harmonize its people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity when the former kings instructed the realm, none failed to guide it with the Odes and Documents, teach it with the Rites and Music, transform its customs, and harmonize its people.

sentences.zh: 故恭儉莊敬而不煩者，教深於《禮》也；

translations.literal: Thus one who is reverent, frugal, dignified, and respectful without being troubled--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Rites;
translations.idiomatic: Thus one who is reverent, frugal, dignified, and respectful without being troubled--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Rites;

sentences.zh: 廣博易良而不奢者，教深于《樂》也；

translations.literal: one who is broad, easy, good, and unpretentious without being extravagant--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Music;
translations.idiomatic: one who is broad, easy, good, and unpretentious without being extravagant--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Music;

sentences.zh: 溫柔敦厚而不愚者，教深於《詩》也；

translations.literal: one who is gentle, yielding, generous, and substantial without being foolish--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Odes;
translations.idiomatic: one who is gentle, yielding, generous, and substantial without being foolish--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Odes;

sentences.zh: 疏通知遠而不誣者，教深於《書》也；

translations.literal: one who is perspicacious, knowing, and far-reaching without being deceitful--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: one who is perspicacious, knowing, and far-reaching without being deceitful--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Documents;

sentences.zh: 潔靜精微而不賊者，教深于《易》也；

translations.literal: one who is pure, quiet, subtle, and refined without being harmful--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Changes;
translations.idiomatic: one who is pure, quiet, subtle, and refined without being harmful--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Changes;

sentences.zh: 屬辭比事而不亂者，教深於《春秋》也。

translations.literal: one who connects words and compares events without confusion--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: one who connects words and compares events without confusion--such teaching has penetrated deeply into the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 夫《樂》以和神，《詩》以正言，《禮》以明體，《書》以廣聽，《春秋》以斷事。

translations.literal: Music harmonizes the spirit; the Odes rectify speech; the Rites clarify form; the Documents broaden hearing; the Spring and Autumn adjudicate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Music harmonizes the spirit; the Odes rectify speech; the Rites clarify form; the Documents broaden hearing; the Spring and Autumn adjudicate affairs.

sentences.zh: 五者，蓋五常之道，相須而備。

translations.literal: These five are essentially the Way of the Five Constants--they depend on one another and are complete together.
translations.idiomatic: These five are essentially the Way of the Five Constants--they depend on one another and are complete together.

sentences.zh: 《易》為之源，故曰《易》不可見，則乾坤其幾乎息矣。

translations.literal: The Changes is their source. Thus it is said: "If the Changes cannot be seen, then Heaven and Earth are nearly at rest."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes is their source. Thus it is said: "If the Changes cannot be seen, then Heaven and Earth are nearly at rest."

sentences.zh: 由是言之，《六經》者，先王之遺烈，聖人之盛事也，安可不遊心寓目習性文身哉！

translations.literal: From this it follows that the Six Classics are the luminous legacy of the former kings and the grand achievement of the sages. How can one fail to fix the mind upon them, give them one's attention, cultivate one's nature through them, and adorn oneself with their text!
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the Six Classics are the luminous legacy of the former kings and the grand achievement of the sages. How can one fail to fix the mind upon them, give them one's attention, cultivate one's nature through them, and adorn oneself with their text!

sentences.zh: 頃因暇日，屬意藝林，略撰所聞，討論其本，名曰《六經略注》，以訓門徒焉！

translations.literal: Recently, on leisure days, I have devoted myself to the grove of learning, briefly setting down what I have heard and examining its foundations. I call it Summary Notes on the Six Classics, to instruct my disciples!
translations.idiomatic: Recently, on leisure days, I have devoted myself to the grove of learning, briefly setting down what I have heard and examining its foundations. I call it Summary Notes on the Six Classics, to instruct my disciples!

sentences.zh: 其《略注》行於世。

translations.literal: The Summary Notes circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The Summary Notes circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 爽不事王侯，獨守閒靜，講肄經典二十餘年，時號為「儒林先生」。

translations.literal: Shuang did not serve princes and nobles, keeping to quiet seclusion, lecturing on the classics for more than twenty years. He was known in his time as the "Scholar of the Forest of Ru."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang did not serve princes and nobles, keeping to quiet seclusion and lecturing on the classics for more than twenty years. He was known in his time as "Master Scholar of the Forest."

sentences.zh: 年六十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty-three he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of sixty-three he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子文通，曆官至鎮西司馬、南天水太守、西翼校尉。

translations.literal: His son Wentong rose through the ranks to Marshal of the Army Who Guards the West, Governor of Southern Tianshui, and Commandant of the Western Wing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wentong rose through the ranks to Marshal of the Army Who Guards the West, Governor of Southern Tianshui, and Commandant of the Western Wing.

sentences.zh: 文通子景。

translations.literal: Wentong had a son Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong had a son Jing.

sentences.zh: 景字永昌，少聰敏，初讀《論語》、《毛詩》，一受便覽。

translations.literal: Jing, styled Yongchang, was clever from youth; when he first read the Analects and Mao's Odes, one reading was enough for him to comprehend them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, styled Yongchang, was clever from youth; when he first read the Analects and Mao's Odes, one reading was enough for him to comprehend them.

sentences.zh: 及長，有才思，雅好文章。

translations.literal: When grown, he had literary talent and loved composition.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he had literary talent and loved composition.

sentences.zh: 廷尉公孫良舉為協律博士，孝文親得其名，既而用之為門下錄事。

translations.literal: Court Commandant Gongsun Liang recommended him as Doctor of Harmonious Music. Emperor Xiaowen personally learned his name and soon after employed him as Recorder in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Court Commandant Gongsun Liang recommended him as Doctor of Harmonious Music. Emperor Xiaowen personally learned his name and soon after employed him as Recorder in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正始初，招尚書、門下于金墉中書外省考論律令，敕景參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi, the Secretariat and the Secretariat Drafting Office were summoned to the Outer Secretariat at Jinyong to examine and discuss statutes and commands; the emperor ordered Jing to participate in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengshi, the Secretariat and the Secretariat Drafting Office were summoned to the Outer Secretariat at Jinyong to examine and discuss statutes and commands; the emperor ordered Jing to participate in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 宣武季舅護軍將軍高顯卒，其兄右僕射肇托景及尚書邢巒、并州刺史高聰、通直郎徐紇各作碑銘，並以呈禦。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu's younger maternal uncle, General Who Protects the Army Gao Xian, died. His elder brother Vice Director Gao Zhao entrusted Jing along with Secretariat Minister Xing Luan, Governor of Bingzhou Gao Cong, and Court Gentleman for Direct Transmission Xu He each to compose an epitaph--all were submitted to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu's younger maternal uncle, General Who Protects the Army Gao Xian, died. His elder brother Vice Director Gao Zhao entrusted Jing along with Secretariat Minister Xing Luan, Governor of Bingzhou Gao Cong, and Court Gentleman for Direct Transmission Xu He each to compose an epitaph--all were submitted to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝悉付侍中崔光簡之，光奏景名位乃處諸人之下，文出諸人之上，遂以景文刊石。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted them all to Attendant Within Cui Guang for selection. Guang reported that though Jing's rank and position were below the others, his text surpassed them all, and so Jing's composition was carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted them all to Attendant Within Cui Guang for selection. Guang reported that though Jing's rank and position were below the others, his writing surpassed them all, and so Jing's text was carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 肇尚平陽公主，未幾主薨，肇欲使公主家令居廬制服，已付學官議正施行。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao had married the Princess of Pingyang. Before long the princess died. Gao Zhao wished to have the princess's household steward observe mourning in a hut and wear mourning garments--this had already been submitted to the scholar-officials for deliberation to determine proper implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao had married the Princess of Pingyang. Before long the princess died. Gao Zhao wished to have the princess's household steward observe mourning in a hut and wear mourning garments--this had already been submitted to the scholar-officials for deliberation to determine proper implementation.

sentences.zh: 尚書又以訪景，景以婦人無專國之理，家令不得有純臣之義，乃執議曰：

translations.literal: The Secretariat again consulted Jing. Jing held that a woman cannot hold exclusive authority over the state, and a household steward cannot bear the full loyalty owed by a pure minister. He therefore submitted an opinion, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat again consulted Jing. Jing held that a woman cannot hold exclusive authority over the state, and a household steward cannot bear the full loyalty owed by a pure minister. He therefore submitted an opinion, saying:

sentences.zh: 喪紀之本，實稱物以立情；

translations.literal: The foundation of mourning regulations truly lies in matching external form to inner feeling;
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of mourning regulations truly lies in matching external form to inner feeling;

sentences.zh: 輕重所因，亦緣情以制禮。

translations.literal: The grounds for lighter and heavier mourning likewise depend on feeling to regulate ritual.
translations.idiomatic: What makes mourning lighter or heavier likewise arises from feeling and is shaped into ritual.

sentences.zh: 雖理關盛衰，事經今古，而製作之本，降殺之宜，其實一焉。

translations.literal: Though the principle bears upon rise and decline and the matter has passed through ancient and modern times, the foundation of formulation and the fitness of gradation are in essence one.
translations.idiomatic: Though the principle touches prosperity and decline and the matter runs through past and present, the root of ritual design and the propriety of graduated mourning are fundamentally the same.

sentences.zh: 是故臣之為君，所以資敬而崇重；

translations.literal: Therefore a subject serving a lord is so as to supply reverence and enhance esteem;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when a subject serves a lord, it is to furnish reverence and heighten respect;

sentences.zh: 為君母妻，所以從服而制義。

translations.literal: serving a lord's mother or wife is so as to follow mourning garments and establish propriety.
translations.idiomatic: and when one serves a lord's mother or wife, it is to follow mourning garments and fix the rules of propriety.

sentences.zh: 然而諸侯大夫之君者，謂其有地土、有吏屬，無服文者，言其非世爵也。

translations.literal: Yet when one speaks of a lord for feudal lords and grand masters, it means one possessing territory and official subordinates; where there are no mourning prescriptions it means the position is not a hereditary fief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the "lord" of feudal lords and grand masters refers to one who holds land and commands officials; where no mourning text applies, it shows the rank is not a hereditary fief.

sentences.zh: 今王姬降適，雖加爵命，事非君邑，理異列土。

translations.literal: Now when an imperial princess marries down, though ennobled with titles and commands, the matter is not that of a lord's domain; the principle differs from holding a fief.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when an imperial princess marries into a lesser house, though she receives titles and honors, this is not the case of a lord's fief; the principle differs from holding landed rank.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 諸王開國，備立臣吏，生有趨奉之勤，死盡致喪之禮。

translations.literal: When feudal princes establish their states, they fully set up ministerial officials--in life there is the duty of attendance and service; in death there is the fullest observance of mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When princes of the blood establish their states, they appoint a full staff of ministers: in life there is the labor of attendance; in death the full rites of mourning.

sentences.zh: 而公主家令，唯有一人，其丞已下，命之屬官，既無接事之儀，實闕為臣之體。

translations.literal: But for a princess's household steward there is only one person; below the assistant are appointed subordinate officials who have neither the ritual of receiving duties nor truly possess the form of serving as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a princess's household steward is a single officer; the assistants and subordinates below him have no ritual of receiving office and lack the substance of ministerial service.

sentences.zh: 原夫公主之貴，所以立家令者，蓋以主之內事，脫須關外，理無自達，必也因人。

translations.literal: Considering why a princess's nobility warrants establishing a household steward: it is because the princess's domestic affairs, should they need to reach outside, cannot by principle be conveyed directly and must rely on another person.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on why a princess of rank needs a household steward: her domestic affairs, if they must reach beyond the household, cannot by nature be handled directly and must pass through another.

sentences.zh: 然則家令唯通內外之職及典主家之事耳，無關君臣之理，名義之分也。

translations.literal: Thus the household steward merely serves to link inner and outer affairs and manage the lady's household--it has nothing to do with the principle of lord and subject or the distinction of title and status.
translations.idiomatic: The steward therefore only mediates between inner and outer affairs and manages the princess's household; he has no bearing on the relation of lord and subject or on the distinction of names and ranks.

sentences.zh: 由是推之，家令不得為純臣，公主不可為正君，明矣。

translations.literal: From this it follows clearly that the household steward cannot be a pure minister, and the princess cannot be a proper lord.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that the steward cannot be a full minister, nor can the princess be a true lord.

sentences.zh: 且女人之為君，男子之為臣，古禮所不載，先朝所未議。

translations.literal: Moreover, a woman as lord and a man as subject is not recorded in ancient ritual, nor was it ever debated by previous dynasties.
