translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, a woman serving as lord with a man as subject appears nowhere in ancient ritual and was never discussed by earlier courts.

sentences.zh: 而四門博士裴道廣、孫榮乂等以公主為之君，以家令為之臣，制服以斬，乖繆彌甚。

translations.literal: Yet Erudites of the Four Gates Pei Daoguang, Sun Rongyi, and others treat the princess as their lord and the household steward as their subject and prescribe the highest grade of mourning--an error all the more gross.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Erudites of the Four Gates Pei Daoguang, Sun Rongyi, and others make the princess their lord and the steward their subject and prescribe the heaviest mourning--a distortion all the worse.

sentences.zh: 又張虛景、吾難羈等不推君臣之分，不尋致服之情，猶同其議，准母制齊，求之名實，理未為允。

translations.literal: Furthermore Zhang Xujing, Wu Nanji, and others, without weighing the lord-subject distinction or seeking the grounds for mourning obligations, still agree with that view and apply mourning on the model of a mother with qi-grade garments-- judged by name and reality, this is not acceptable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xujing, Wu Nanji, and others likewise fail to consider the lord-subject distinction or the grounds for mourning, yet follow that opinion and apply mourning as for a mother in qi garments-- judged by name and fact, this cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 竊謂公主之爵，既非食采之君；

translations.literal: I venture to say that the princess's rank is not that of a lord who receives a fief;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that a princess's title is not the rank of a fief-holding lord;

sentences.zh: 家令之官，又無純臣之式。

translations.literal: and the office of household steward lacks the form of a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: and the office of household steward has no model of a full minister.

sentences.zh: 若附如母，則情議罔施；

translations.literal: If one treats it as toward a mother, emotional justification cannot be applied;
translations.idiomatic: If one treats the case like a mother, feeling and reason cannot be applied;

sentences.zh: 若准小君，則從服無據。

translations.literal: if one follows the model of a lesser lady of the house, there is no basis for derived mourning.
translations.idiomatic: if one follows the model of a lesser lady of the house, there is no ground for derived mourning.

sentences.zh: 案如經《禮》，事無成文，即之愚見，謂不應服。

translations.literal: According to the canonical "Rituals," there is no established precedent for this matter; in my humble view, mourning should not be worn.
translations.idiomatic: According to the canonical "Rituals," no established rule covers this case; in my humble opinion, mourning ought not to be worn.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 景淹滯門下積歲，不至顯官，以蜀司馬相如、王褒、嚴君平、揚子雲等四賢，皆有高才而無重位，乃托意以贊之。

translations.literal: Jing lingered at the Secretariat Gate for many years without reaching a prominent post; taking Sima Xiangru, Wang Bao, Yan Junping, and Yang Ziyun--four worthies of Shu, all possessed of great talent yet without high rank--he expressed his meaning through praise of them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing remained at the Secretariat Gate for years without rising to a high office. Thinking of four men of Shu--Sima Xiangru, Wang Bao, Yan Junping, and Yang Ziyun--all gifted yet never granted great rank, he poured his feelings into praise of them.

sentences.zh: 景在樞密十有餘年，為侍中崔光、盧昶、遊肇、元暉尤所知賞。

translations.literal: Jing spent more than ten years in confidential service and was especially recognized and esteemed by Attendants Within Cui Guang, Lu Chang, You Zhao, and Yuan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years Jing served in the inner councils and won particular recognition from Attendants Within Cui Guang, Lu Chang, You Zhao, and Yuan Ye.

sentences.zh: 累遷積射將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General Who Shoots Rapidly and Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to General Who Shoots Rapidly and Supervisor of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，東宮建，兼太子屯騎校尉，錄事皆如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang, when the Eastern Palace was established, he was additionally appointed Commandant of Cavalry of Crown Prince Retinue while his duties as Recorder remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanchang, when the Eastern Palace was established, he was also made Commandant of Cavalry of the Crown Prince Retinue while continuing as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 受敕撰門下詔書凡四十卷。

translations.literal: He received orders to compile forty volumes of Secretariat Gate edicts.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he compiled forty volumes of edicts from the Secretariat Gate.

sentences.zh: 尚書元萇出為安西將軍、雍州刺史，請景為司馬。

translations.literal: Secretariat Minister Yuan Chang went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province and requested Jing as his Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Secretariat Minister Yuan Chang was posted as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province, he asked that Jing serve as his Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 以景階次不及，除錄事參軍、襄威將軍，帶長安令，甚有惠政，人吏稱之。

translations.literal: Because Jing's rank was not yet sufficient, he was appointed Recording Secretary and General Who Spreads Might, concurrently serving as Magistrate of Chang'an; he administered with considerable benevolence, and officials and commoners praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jing's rank was still too low for that post, he was made Recording Secretary and General Who Spreads Might, concurrently Magistrate of Chang'an. He governed with notable kindness, and officials and people alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 先是，太常劉芳與景等撰朝令，未及班行。

translations.literal: Earlier, Court Director Liu Fang together with Jing and others had compiled court ordinances but had not yet issued them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Court Director Liu Fang, Jing, and others had drafted court ordinances that had not yet been promulgated.

sentences.zh: 別典儀注，多所草創，未成。

translations.literal: Separate canonical ritual regulations had been largely drafted but not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Separate ritual codes had also been largely drafted but left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 芳卒，景纂成其事。

translations.literal: When Liu Fang died, Jing compiled and completed the work.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Fang died, Jing gathered the materials and finished the work.

sentences.zh: 及宣武崩，召景赴京，還修儀注。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Jing was summoned to the capital and returned to revising the ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Jing was called to the capital and resumed editing the ritual codes.

sentences.zh: 拜謁者僕射，加甯遠將軍，又以本官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Master of Ceremonial Attendants and promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant, and with his existing office he also served concurrently as Secretariat Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Master of Ceremonial Attendants and General Who Pacifies the Distant, and continued concurrently as Secretariat Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後授步兵校尉，仍舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was given the post of Commandant of Foot Soldiers while retaining his attendant status.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the post of Commandant of Foot Soldiers while remaining an attendant.

sentences.zh: 又敕撰太和之後朝儀已施行者，凡五十餘卷。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to compile court rituals implemented since the Taihe era, more than fifty volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered to compile the court rituals put into practice since the Taihe era, more than fifty volumes in total.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后詔依漢世陰、鄧二後故事，親奉廟祀，與帝交獻。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Ling ordered that, following the precedents of Empresses Yin and Deng of the Han, she should personally attend temple sacrifices and alternate offerings with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Ling ordered that, following Han precedents of Empresses Yin and Deng, she would personally attend temple sacrifices and alternate offerings with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 景乃據正以定儀注，朝廷是之。

translations.literal: Jing then determined the ritual regulations on orthodox grounds, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then fixed the ritual regulations on orthodox grounds, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 正光初，除龍驤將軍、中散大夫，舍人如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang, he was appointed General Who Dragon-Prances and Palace Attendant, while his attendant duties continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguang he was appointed General Who Dragon-Prances and Palace Attendant, retaining his attendant duties.

sentences.zh: 時明帝行講學之禮于國子寺，司徒崔光執經，敕景與董紹、張徹、馮元興、王延業、鄭伯猷等俱為錄義。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming performed the lecture ritual at the Imperial Academy; Minister of Works Cui Guang held the classics, and Jing was ordered together with Dong Shao, Zhang Che, Feng Yuanxing, Wang Yanye, and Zheng Boyou to record the exposition.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ming performed the lecture rite at the Imperial Academy. Minister of Works Cui Guang expounded the classics, and Jing was ordered, together with Dong Shao, Zhang Che, Feng Yuanxing, Wang Yanye, and Zheng Boyou, to record the discussion.

sentences.zh: 事畢，又行釋奠之禮，並詔百官作釋奠詩，以景作為美。

translations.literal: When that was done, the libation ceremony was also performed, and all officials were ordered to compose libation poetry; Jing's composition was judged the finest.
translations.idiomatic: When that was finished, the libation ceremony was also held, and all officials were ordered to compose libation poems; Jing's was judged the best.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，蠕蠕主阿那瑰歸闕，朝廷疑其位次。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month, the Rouran chief Anagui returned to court, and the court was uncertain about his seating order.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the ninth month the Rouran chief Anagui came to court, and the court was unsure where to place him in the seating order.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍訪景。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong consulted Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gaoyang, Yuan Yong, asked Jing's opinion.

sentences.zh: 曰：「昔咸甯中，南單于來朝，晉世處之王公、特進之下。

translations.literal: He said: "In the Xianning era, when the Southern Chanyu came to court, the Jin placed him below dukes and grandees and those of special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "In the Xianning era, when the Southern Chanyu came to court, the Jin seated him below dukes, grandees, and holders of special advancement.

sentences.zh: 今日為班，宜在蕃王、儀同三司之間。

translations.literal: For today's seating order, he should be placed between royal princes of foreign origin and Honorary Commanders-in-Chief of Three Armies."
translations.idiomatic: For today's order of precedence, he should be placed between foreign princes and Honorary Commanders-in-Chief of Three Armies."

sentences.zh: 」雍從之。

translations.literal: " Yong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong took his advice.

sentences.zh: 朝廷典章，疑而不決，則時訪景而行。

translations.literal: Whenever court institutions were in doubt and could not be decided, the court would consult Jing before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court ritual was uncertain and could not be settled, the court would consult Jing before acting.

sentences.zh: 初，平齊之後，光祿大夫高聰徙於北京，中書監高允為之聘妻，給其資宅。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the pacification of Qi, Grand Master of Splendor Gao Cong was relocated to the Northern Capital; Secretariat Director Gao Yun arranged a marriage for him and provided a residence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Qi was pacified, Grand Master of Splendor Gao Cong was moved to the Northern Capital; Secretariat Director Gao Yun found him a wife and supplied a house.

sentences.zh: 聰後為允立碑，每云「吾以此文報德足矣。

translations.literal: Later Cong erected a stele for Yun, often saying: "With this text I have repaid his kindness sufficiently.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cong erected a stele for Yun and often said: "With this inscription I have repaid his kindness enough.

sentences.zh: 」豫州刺史常綽以未盡其美。

translations.literal: " Governor of Yuzhou Chang Chuo felt it had not fully captured Yun's virtues.
translations.idiomatic: " Governor of Yuzhou Chang Chuo felt it did not fully express Yun's virtues.

sentences.zh: 景尚允才器，先為《遺德頌》，司徒崔光聞而觀之，尋味良久，乃云：「高光祿平日每矜其文，自許報允之德，今見常生此頌，高氏不得獨擅其美也。

translations.literal: Jing admired Yun's talent and had previously composed "An Ode to His Transmitted Virtue." Minister of Works Cui Guang heard of it and read it; after savoring it for a long while he said: "Master Gao the Grand Master of Splendor always prided himself on his writing and claimed it repaid Yun's kindness--now that I see Master Chang's ode, the Gao family can no longer monopolize the praise.
translations.idiomatic: Jing admired Yun's talent and had already written "An Ode to His Transmitted Virtue." Minister of Works Cui Guang heard of it and read the piece; after pondering it for a long time he said: "Master Gao the Grand Master of Splendor always prided himself on his prose and claimed it repaid Yun's kindness--now that I see Master Chang's ode, the Gao family can no longer keep the praise to themselves.

sentences.zh: 」侍中崔光、安豐王延明受詔議定服章，敕景參修其事。

translations.literal: " Attendants Within Cui Guang and Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming were ordered to deliberate and fix ceremonial attire, and Jing was directed to participate in revising the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendants Within Cui Guang and Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming were ordered to deliberate on ceremonial dress, and Jing was directed to help revise the regulations.

sentences.zh: 尋進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was advanced to the title General Who Champions the State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to General Who Champions the State.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰之還國也，境上遷延，仍陳窘乏。

translations.literal: When Anagui was returning to his country, he lingered at the border and again pleaded poverty and want.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui was returning home, he delayed at the frontier and again pleaded hardship and poverty.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書左丞元孚奉詔振恤，阿那瑰執孚過柔玄，奔於漠北。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant of the Secretariat Yuan Fu was sent with an imperial edict to provide relief, but Anagui seized Fu and passed through Rouxuan, fleeing into the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant of the Secretariat Yuan Fu was sent with an edict to provide relief, but Anagui seized him, passed through Rouxuan, and fled into the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書令李崇、御史中尉兼右僕射元纂追討不及。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Chong and Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Vice Director Yuan Zuan were sent in pursuit but failed to catch him.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Chong and Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Vice Director Yuan Zuan were sent in pursuit but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 乃令景出塞，經絺山，臨瀚海，宣敕勒眾而返。

translations.literal: Jing was then ordered to go beyond the frontier, pass through Qishan, reach the Hanhai, proclaim the edict, rally the troops, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was then ordered to go beyond the frontier, pass Qishan, reach the Hanhai, proclaim the edict, rally the troops, and return.

sentences.zh: 景經涉山水，悵然懷古，乃擬劉琨《扶風歌》十二首。

translations.literal: As Jing traversed mountains and rivers, he was filled with melancholy and turned to antiquity, composing twelve pieces in imitation of Liu Kun's "Fufeng Songs."
translations.idiomatic: Crossing mountains and rivers, Jing was moved to melancholy and looked back to antiquity, composing twelve poems after the manner of Liu Kun's "Fufeng Songs."

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，給事黃門侍郎，尋除左將軍、太府少卿，仍舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in the Yellow Gate Service, and soon after was made Left General and Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse while retaining his attendant duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaochang he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in the Yellow Gate Service; soon after he was made Left General and Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse while continuing as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 固辭少卿不拜，改授散騎常侍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the vice directorship and did not accept it; he was reassigned as Regular Attendant and his generalship remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the vice directorship and refused the appointment; he was reassigned Regular Attendant, and his generalship remained as before.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史元法僧叛入梁，梁武遣其豫章王蕭綜入據彭城。

translations.literal: Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng rebelled and fled to Liang; Emperor Wu of Liang sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zong, to enter and hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng rebelled and went over to Liang; Emperor Wu of Liang sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zong, to enter and occupy Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時安豐王延明為大都督、大行台，率臨淮王彧等眾軍討之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming was Grand Commander and Grand Mobile Headquarters, leading the armies of Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming served as Grand Commander and Grand Mobile Headquarters, leading the armies of Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu and others against them.

sentences.zh: 既而蕭綜降附，徐州清復，遣景兼尚書，持節馳與行台都督觀機部分。

translations.literal: Before long Xiao Zong surrendered, Xuzhou was cleared and restored, and Jing was sent as Acting Secretariat Minister bearing credentials to ride post-haste and coordinate with the Mobile Headquarters commander as circumstances dictated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Zong surrendered, Xuzhou was recovered, and Jing was sent as Acting Secretariat Minister with credentials to ride post-haste and join the Mobile Headquarters commander in directing operations as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 景經洛納，乃作銘焉。

translations.literal: Passing through Luona, Jing composed an inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed Luona, Jing composed an inscription.

sentences.zh: 是時尚書令蕭寶夤、都督崔延伯、都督北海王顥、都督車騎將軍元恆芝等並各出討，詔景詣軍宣旨勞問。

translations.literal: At that time Secretariat Director Xiao Baoyin, Commander Cui Yanbo, Commander Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao, Commander General of Chariots and Cavalry Yuan Hengzhi, and others each went out on campaign; Jing was ordered to visit the armies to proclaim the imperial will and convey consolation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Secretariat Director Xiao Baoyin, Commander Cui Yanbo, Commander Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao, Commander General of Chariots and Cavalry Yuan Hengzhi, and others each marched out on campaign; Jing was ordered to visit the armies, proclaim the imperial will, and convey the court's regard.

sentences.zh: 還，以本將軍授徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On his return he was given the governorship of Xuzhou with his existing generalship.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou while retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: b杜洛周反于燕州，仍以景兼尚書為行台，與幽州都督、平北將軍元譚以禦之。

translations.literal: Du Luozhou rebelled in Yan Province; Jing was again made Acting Secretariat Minister as Mobile Headquarters to join with Yan Province Commander and General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Tan in resisting him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou rebelled in Yan Province; Jing was again made Acting Secretariat Minister and Mobile Headquarters commander to join Yan Province Commander and General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Tan in resisting him.

sentences.zh: 景表求勒幽州諸縣悉入古城，山路有通賊之處，權發兵夫，隨宜置戍，以為防遏。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial requesting that all counties of You Province be urged to enter the old walled cities; wherever mountain roads allowed passage for bandits, laborers and troops should be dispatched as needed and garrisons established for defense and blocking.
translations.idiomatic: Jing submitted a memorial asking that all counties in You Province be urged into the old walled cities; wherever mountain paths gave bandits passage, troops and laborers should be dispatched as needed and garrisons set up to block them.

sentences.zh: 又以頃來差兵，不盡強壯，今之三長，綿是豪門多丁為之，今求權發為兵。

translations.literal: He also noted that recently conscripted soldiers had not all been strong and able, and that the current three-elder system was largely staffed by powerful clans with many sons; he requested authority to conscript them as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that recent levies had not produced enough strong men, and that the three-elder posts were now largely filled by powerful clans with many sons; he asked permission to conscript them for military service.

sentences.zh: 明帝皆從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming approved everything.

sentences.zh: 進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 別敕譚西至軍都關，北從盧龍塞，據此二險，以杜賊出入之路。

translations.literal: A separate edict ordered Tan to go west to Jundu Pass and north from Lulong Pass, holding these two strongpoints to block the bandits' routes of entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict ordered Tan west to Jundu Pass and north through Lulong Pass, holding these two strongpoints to cut off the bandits' routes in and out.

sentences.zh: 又詔景山中險路之處，悉令捍塞。

translations.literal: Jing was also ordered to block every perilous mountain route.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was also ordered to block every dangerous mountain pass.

sentences.zh: 景遣府錄事參軍裴智成發范陽三長之兵以守白曵閏，都督元譚據居庸下口。

translations.literal: Jing sent his Recording Secretary Pei Zhicheng to mobilize the three-elder militia of Fanyang to hold Baiye Pass, while Commander Yuan Tan held the lower mouth of Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent his Recording Secretary Pei Zhicheng to raise the three-elder militia of Fanyang to hold Baiye Pass, while Commander Yuan Tan held the lower mouth of Juyong.

sentences.zh: 俄而安州石離、冗城、斛鹽三戍兵反，結洛周，有眾二萬餘落，自松岍赴賊。

translations.literal: Soon garrison soldiers at Shili, Rongcheng, and Huyan in An Province rebelled, joined with Luozhou, mustered more than twenty thousand households, and marched from Songqian to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison troops at Shili, Rongcheng, and Huyan in An Province rebelled, joined Luozhou, gathered more than twenty thousand households, and marched from Songqian to join the rebels.

sentences.zh: 譚勒別將崔仲哲等截軍都關以待之。

translations.literal: Tan ordered subordinate general Cui Zhongzhe and others to intercept at Jundu Pass and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan ordered subordinate general Cui Zhongzhe and others to block Jundu Pass and wait for them.

sentences.zh: 仲哲戰沒，洛周又自外應之，腹背受敵，譚遂大敗，諸軍夜散。

translations.literal: Zhongzhe died in battle; Luozhou also responded from outside, Tan was caught between two fronts and suffered a great defeat, and the armies dispersed by night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhe fell in battle; Luozhou also answered from outside, Tan was caught between two enemies and suffered a crushing defeat, and the armies broke up in the night.

sentences.zh: 詔以景所部別將李琚為都督，代譚征下口，降景為後將軍，解州任。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li Ju, a subordinate general under Jing, as commander to replace Tan in campaigning at the lower pass; Jing was demoted to Rear General and relieved of his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Li Ju, a subordinate general under Jing, commander in Tan's place at the lower pass; Jing was demoted to Rear General and relieved of his provincial post.

sentences.zh: 仍詔景為幽、安、玄四州行台。

translations.literal: Jing was still appointed Mobile Headquarters over the four provinces of You, An, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was nevertheless appointed Mobile Headquarters commander over the four provinces including You, An, and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 賊既南出，鈔略薊城，景命統軍梁仲禮率兵士邀擊。

translations.literal: After the bandits moved south and raided Ji City, Jing ordered Commander Liang Zhongli to lead troops and intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits moved south and raided Ji City, Jing ordered Commander Liang Zhongli to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 破之，獲賊將禦夷鎮軍主孫念恆。

translations.literal: They defeated them and captured the bandit general Defender of Yuyi Garrison Commander Sun Nianheng.
translations.idiomatic: They routed them and captured the bandit general Defender of Yuyi Garrison Commander Sun Nianheng.

sentences.zh: 都督李琚為賊所攻薊城之北，軍敗而死。

translations.literal: Commander Li Ju was attacked by bandits north of Ji City; his army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Ju was attacked by bandits north of Ji City, his force was defeated, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 率屬城人禦之，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jing led the people of subordinate cities to resist them, and the bandits did not dare press closer.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led the people of the dependent cities to resist, and the bandits did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 洛周還據上穀。

translations.literal: Luozhou returned to occupy Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou withdrew to hold Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 授景平北將軍、光祿大夫，行台如故。

translations.literal: Jing was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Splendor, with Mobile Headquarters unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was made General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Splendor, and retained his Mobile Headquarters post.

sentences.zh: 洛周遣其都督王曹紇真、馬叱斤等率眾薊南，以掠人穀，乃遇連雨，賊眾疲勞。

translations.literal: Luozhou sent his commanders Wang Cao Gezhen, Ma Chijin, and others to lead troops south of Ji to plunder grain and people; they encountered continuous rain, and the bandit force grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou sent his commanders Wang Cao Gezhen, Ma Chijin, and others south of Ji with troops to seize grain and captives; they met with days of rain, and the bandit force grew exhausted.

sentences.zh: 景與都督于榮、制史王延年置兵栗國，邀其走路，大敗之，斬曹紇真。

translations.literal: Jing together with Commander Yu Rong and Inspector Wang Yannian stationed troops at Liguo, intercepted their route, inflicted a great defeat, and killed Cao Gezhen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, together with Commander Yu Rong and Inspector Wang Yannian, set troops at Liguo, cut off their line of retreat, routed them, and killed Cao Gezhen.

sentences.zh: 洛周率眾南趨范陽，景與延年及榮破之。

translations.literal: Luozhou led his force south toward Fanyang; Jing together with Yannian and Rong defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou led his force south toward Fanyang; Jing, Yannian, and Rong defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又遣別將重破之於州西彪眼泉，禽斬之及溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: He also sent a subordinate general to again defeat them at Biaoyan Spring west of the province; many were captured, killed, or drowned.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a subordinate general to defeat them again at Biaoyan Spring west of the province; a great many were captured, killed, or drowned.

sentences.zh: 後洛周南圍范陽，城人翻降，執刺史延年及景，送于洛周。

translations.literal: Later Luozhou besieged Fanyang from the south; the city people mutinied and surrendered, seized Governor Yannian and Jing, and delivered them to Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Luozhou besieged Fanyang from the south; the townspeople turned and surrendered, seized Governor Yannian and Jing, and handed them over to Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為葛榮所吞，景又入榮。

translations.literal: Before long Luozhou was absorbed by Ge Rong, and Jing likewise came under Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luozhou was swallowed up by Ge Rong, and Jing passed into Rong's camp as well.

sentences.zh: 榮破，景得還朝。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was defeated, Jing was able to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was broken, Jing was able to return to court.

sentences.zh: 永安初，詔復本官，兼黃門侍郎，又攝著作，固辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan an edict restored his former offices and additionally made him Attendant in the Yellow Gate Service and acting Director of Compilation; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongan an edict restored his former posts and additionally made him Attendant in the Yellow Gate Service and acting Director of Compilation; he firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 二年，除中軍將軍，正黃門。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Central Army General and Regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Central Army General and Regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 先是參議《正光壬子曆》，至是賜爵高陽子。

translations.literal: He had previously participated in deliberating the "Zhenguang Rensi Calendar"; at this time he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier taken part in deliberating the "Zhenguang Rensi Calendar"; at this time he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 元顥內逼，莊帝北巡，景與侍中、大司馬、安豐王延明在禁中召諸親賓，乃安慰京師。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang toured north; Jing together with Attendant Within, Grand Marshal, and Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming summoned kinsmen and guests within the palace precincts and thus reassured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang went north on tour; Jing, together with Attendant Within, Grand Marshal, and Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming, summoned kinsmen and guests within the palace and thus steadied the capital.

sentences.zh: 顥入洛，景乃居本位。

translations.literal: When Hao entered Luoyang, Jing resumed his proper posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao entered Luoyang, Jing returned to his proper offices.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，解黃門。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Jing was relieved of his Yellow Gate duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Jing was relieved of his Yellow Gate post.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除車騎將軍、右光祿大夫、秘書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Grand Master of Splendor, and Director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Putai he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Grand Master of Splendor, and Director of the Secretariat Library.

sentences.zh: 以預詔命之勤，封濮陽縣子，後以例追。

translations.literal: For his diligence in drafting imperial edicts beforehand, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puyang County; later this was revoked according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For his diligence in preparing imperial edicts in advance, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puyang County; later the title was rescinded according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，監議事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he supervised deliberative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, he served as overseer of deliberative affairs.

sentences.zh: 景善與人交，終始若一。

translations.literal: Jing was good in associating with people, from beginning to end as one.
translations.idiomatic: In his dealings with others, Jing was steadfast from first to last.

sentences.zh: 其遊處者皆服其深遠之度，未曾見其矜吝之心。

translations.literal: Those who traveled and kept company with him all submitted to his profound and far-reaching measure; they had never seen a proud and stingy heart in him.
translations.idiomatic: All who kept company with him admired his depth and long perspective; none ever saw in him pride or miserliness.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，淡于榮利，自得懷抱，不事權門。

translations.literal: He loved drinking wine, was indifferent to glory and profit, found contentment within himself, and did not attend to powerful gates.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, cared little for rank and gain, was self-sufficient in spirit, and would not court powerful families.

sentences.zh: 性和厚恭慎。

translations.literal: His nature was harmonious, generous, respectful, and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: His character was gentle, sincere, and discreetly cautious.

sentences.zh: 每讀書見韋弦之事、深薄之危，乃圖古昔可以鑒戒，指事為象，贊而述之曰：

translations.literal: Whenever in reading he saw the matter of bowstring and mat and the peril of depth and shallowness, he would depict antiquity that could serve as mirror and warning, take affairs as images, and in praise narrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read of the bowstring-at-the-waist and the danger of deep and shallow waters, he would draw lessons from the past for warning and reflection, shape events into emblems, and compose a rhapsody in praise, saying:

sentences.zh: 《周雅》云：「謂天蓋高，不敢不局；

translations.literal: The Odes of Zhou say: 'They say heaven covers high, and one dare not but be bent low;
translations.idiomatic: The Odes of Zhou say: 'Heaven, we are told, stretches overhead, and none dares fail to crouch beneath it;

sentences.zh: 謂地蓋厚，不敢不蹐。

translations.literal: they say earth covers thick, and one dare not but tread mincingly.
translations.idiomatic: 'Earth, we are told, lies deep beneath, and none dares fail to walk upon it with care.

sentences.zh: 」有朝隱大夫鑒戒斯文，乃惕焉而懼曰：夫道喪則性傾，利重則身輕。

translations.literal: ' The Court Recluse Grandee took this text as mirror and warning, and thus grew wary and alarmed, saying: When the Way is lost the nature inclines; when profit weighs heavy the body grows light.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Court Recluse Grandee took this as a text for warning and reflection, and in vigilance and fear he said: When the Way is lost, one's nature tilts awry; when profit weighs heavy, one's person grows light.

sentences.zh: 是故乘和體遜，式銘方冊；

translations.literal: Therefore, riding harmony and embodying humility, he inscribes it upon the written records;
translations.idiomatic: So, embracing harmony and the body of humility, he inscribed it in the written records;

sentences.zh: 防微慎獨，載象丹青。

translations.literal: guarding against the subtle and being cautious when alone, he sets images in red and black.
translations.idiomatic: guarded against what is subtle and watched himself in solitude, and placed its images in scarlet and ink.

sentences.zh: 信哉辭人之賦，文晦而理明。

translations.literal: True indeed is the poet's rhapsody: the words obscure yet the principle clear.
translations.idiomatic: How true is the poet's song: the language is indirect, yet the meaning shines clear.

sentences.zh: 仰瞻高天，聽卑視諦；

translations.literal: Looking up to gaze at the lofty heaven, listening low and viewing attentively;
translations.idiomatic: He looked up at the lofty heavens and listened humbly with fixed attention;

sentences.zh: 俯測厚地，嶽峻川渟。

translations.literal: looking down to measure the thick earth, mountains steep and rivers still.
translations.idiomatic: he looked down to measure the deep earth, where peaks rise sharp and rivers lie still.

sentences.zh: 誰共戴之，不私不畏；

translations.literal: Who together bears it? Without partiality, without fear;
translations.idiomatic: Who bears it above us all? It shows no favor, accepts no fear;

sentences.zh: 誰其踐之，不陷不墜。

translations.literal: who treads upon it? Without sinking, without falling.
translations.idiomatic: who walks upon it? He does not sink, does not fall.

sentences.zh: 故善惡是征，物罔同異。

translations.literal: Therefore good and evil are examined, and things share no sameness or difference.
translations.idiomatic: Thus good and evil are tested alike, and nothing escapes distinction.

sentences.zh: 論亢匪久，人咸敬忌。

translations.literal: To discuss exaltation is not for long; people alike revere and fear.
translations.idiomatic: High station cannot long endure in talk alone; all men feel awe and dread toward it.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 唯地厚矣，尚亦兢兢。

translations.literal: Though the earth is thick indeed, still one must be vigilant.
translations.idiomatic: Earth is deep indeed, yet still one must walk with trembling care.

sentences.zh: 浩浩名位，孰識其親。

translations.literal: Vast and boundless are fame and rank--who knows their true kin?
translations.idiomatic: Fame and title spread boundless as the flood--who can say what they truly are?

sentences.zh: 搏之弗得，聆之無聞。

translations.literal: Grasp them and they cannot be obtained; listen and there is nothing heard.
translations.idiomatic: Clutch at them and they slip away; listen, and no sound returns.

sentences.zh: 故有戒於顯而急於微。

translations.literal: Therefore one is warned by what is manifest and urgent about what is subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Hence warning comes from what is plain, urgency from what is small.

sentences.zh: 好爵是冒，聲奢是基。

translations.literal: Fine rank is what is coveted; lavish reputation is the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Men covet noble rank; they build their lives on clamorous fame.

sentences.zh: 身陷於祿利，言溺於是非。

translations.literal: The body sinks in emolument and profit; words drown in right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The body is swallowed by salary and gain; speech is drowned in the quarrels of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 或求欲而未厭，或知足而不辭。

translations.literal: Some pursue desire without being sated; some know sufficiency without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Some crave without ever being satisfied; some know enough yet will not step back.

sentences.zh: 是故位高而勢逾迫，正立而邪逾欺。

translations.literal: Therefore the higher the position the more pressing the power; standing upright, depravity all the more deceives.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the higher one stands, the fiercer power presses in; set on uprightness, yet depravity presses all the closer.

sentences.zh: 安有位朽而危不萃，邪榮而正不雕。

translations.literal: How can there be one whose rank rots yet peril does not gather, whose depravity flourishes yet the upright is not carved away?
translations.idiomatic: When rank rots, peril always gathers; when wickedness prospers, integrity is always cut away.

sentences.zh: 故悔多於地厚，禍甚于天高。

translations.literal: Thus regret exceeds the thickness of earth, and calamity surpasses the height of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Regret runs deeper than the earth; disaster rises higher than heaven.

sentences.zh: 夫悔未結，誰肯曲躬。

translations.literal: When regret has not yet formed, who would willingly bow the body?
translations.idiomatic: Before regret takes root, who will humble himself?

sentences.zh: 夫禍未加，誰肯累足。

translations.literal: When calamity has not yet fallen, who would willingly tread carefully?
translations.idiomatic: Before disaster strikes, who will walk with careful steps?

sentences.zh: 固機發而後思圖，車覆而後改躅。

translations.literal: It is only when the trigger is pulled that one afterward thinks to plan; only when the cart overturns that one afterward changes stride.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the mechanism fires do men think to plan; only after the cart overturns do they change their step.

sentences.zh: 改之無及，故狡兔失穴；

translations.literal: When change comes too late, hence the cunning hare loses its burrow;
translations.idiomatic: When there is no time left to turn back, the clever hare loses its den;

sentences.zh: 思之在後，故逆鱗易觸。

translations.literal: when reflection comes afterward, hence the inverted scale is easy to touch.
translations.idiomatic: when thought comes too late, the dragon's scales are easy to touch and provoke.

sentences.zh: 君子則不然。

translations.literal: The gentleman is not like this.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman does not act like this.

sentences.zh: 體舒則懷卷，視溺則思濟。

translations.literal: When the body is at ease he still holds the scroll; when he sees drowning he thinks of rescue.
translations.idiomatic: At ease he still keeps the book in hand; when he sees another drowning he thinks how to save him.

sentences.zh: 原夫人闕之度，邈於無階之天，勢位之危，深於不測之地。

translations.literal: Considering the measure of human inadequacy--more distant than heaven with no ladder--the peril of power and position, deeper than ground that cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect that human limitation stretches farther than ladderless heaven, and that the peril of power and rank runs deeper than unfathomable earth.

sentences.zh: 餌厚而躬不競，爵降而心不系。

translations.literal: Though bait is thick the body does not compete; though rank descends the heart is not bound.
translations.idiomatic: Though rich bait is offered, his person does not struggle for it; though rank falls away, his heart is not tied down.

sentences.zh: 守善於已成，懼愆於未敗。

translations.literal: He keeps goodness in what is already achieved, and fears fault in what is not yet ruined.
translations.idiomatic: He guards what is already good, and dreads error while nothing has yet gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 雖盈而戒沖，通而慮滯。

translations.literal: Though full he guards against excess; though unimpeded he considers stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Though he is filled, he warns himself against overflowing; though all flows freely, he considers how it may stall.

sentences.zh: 以知命為遐齡，以樂天為大惠。

translations.literal: He takes knowing fate as long life, and taking joy in Heaven as the greatest grace.
translations.idiomatic: He counts knowing one's lot as longevity, and delight in Heaven's order as the deepest blessing.

sentences.zh: 以戢智而從時，以懷愚而遊世。

translations.literal: He restrains wisdom and follows the times; he harbors foolishness and roams the world.
translations.idiomatic: He sheathes his wit and moves with the age; he keeps a store of simplicity and walks through the world.

sentences.zh: 曲躬焉，累足焉，苟行之晝已決矣，猶夜則思其計；

translations.literal: He bows the body, he treads carefully--if by day the course is already decided, still at night he thinks through the plan;
translations.idiomatic: He bends low, he walks with restrained steps; if by day the path is already settled, at night he still weighs the design;

sentences.zh: 誦之口亦明矣，故心必賞其契。

translations.literal: though the mouth recites it clearly, the heart must appreciate its accord.
translations.idiomatic: though his lips speak it plainly, his heart must honor its inner truth.

sentences.zh: 故能不同不誘，而弭謗於群小；

translations.literal: Thus he can be neither different nor enticed, and still quell slander among petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Thus, neither drawn aside nor tempted, he stills the gossip of petty men;

sentences.zh: 無毀無譽，而貽信於上帝。

translations.literal: neither destroyed nor praised, and yet leaves trust with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: neither defamed nor flattered, he yet wins trust from the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 托身與金石俱固，立名與天壤相弊。

translations.literal: He entrusts his person as firm as metal and stone; he establishes his name to end together with heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: He anchors his life in what is hard as metal and stone; he builds a name to perish only with heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 囂競無侵，優遊獨逝。

translations.literal: No clamor or strife invades; he wanders at leisure alone.
translations.idiomatic: Noise and strife cannot touch him; he drifts at ease, alone.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，綺閣金門，可安其宅；

translations.literal: If it is so, brocade halls and golden gates may house his dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: Then brocade chambers and gilded gates may safely hold his home;

sentences.zh: 錦衣玉食，可頤其形。

translations.literal: brocade robes and jade food may nourish his form.
translations.idiomatic: silken robes and jade dishes may rightly sustain his body.

sentences.zh: 柳下三黜，不慍其色；

translations.literal: When Liu Xia was thrice dismissed, he did not darken his countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia Hui was demoted three times, yet his face never darkened;

sentences.zh: 子文三陟，不喜其情。

translations.literal: when Zi Wen thrice ascended, he did not rejoice in feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Wen was raised three times, yet his heart never swelled with joy.

sentences.zh: 而惑者見居高可以持勢，欲乘高以據榮。

translations.literal: But the confused see that occupying height can sustain power, and wish to ride high to seize glory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deluded see that height can hold power, and seek to climb high and seize honor.

sentences.zh: 見直道可以修己，欲專道以邀聲。

translations.literal: They see that the straight Way can cultivate the self, and wish to monopolize the Way to invite renown.
translations.idiomatic: They see that the straight Way can refine the self, and seek to hoard the Way and harvest fame.

sentences.zh: 夫去聲然後聲可立，豈矜道之所宣。

translations.literal: Only when fame is set aside can fame be established--how could one display the Way to proclaim it?
translations.idiomatic: Only when reputation is cast off can a true name stand--how, then, can one vaunt the Way to broadcast oneself?

sentences.zh: 慮危然後安可固，豈假道之所全。

translations.literal: Only when peril is contemplated can safety be secured--how could one borrow the Way to preserve oneself entirely?
translations.idiomatic: Only by foreseeing danger can peace endure--how can one use the Way as a shelter to save oneself whole?

sentences.zh: 是以君子鑒恃道不可以流聲，故去聲而懷道。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman, reflecting that relying on the Way cannot spread fame, sets fame aside and embraces the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman therefore sees that leaning on the Way cannot spread one's name, and so puts fame aside to hold fast to the Way.

sentences.zh: 鑒專道不可以守勢，故去勢以崇道。

translations.literal: Reflecting that monopolizing the Way cannot guard power, he sets power aside to exalt the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that clinging to the Way cannot protect one's power, he relinquishes power to honor the Way.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 履道雖高，不得無亢；

translations.literal: Though treading the Way may be lofty, one cannot be without excess;
translations.idiomatic: To walk the Way is lofty indeed, yet one cannot be free of overbearing pride;

sentences.zh: 求聲雖道，不得無悔。

translations.literal: though seeking fame follows the Way, one cannot be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: to pursue fame, even along the Way, is to invite regret.

sentences.zh: 然則聲奢繁則實儉雕，功業進則身跡退。

translations.literal: Then when reputation grows lavish and complex, substance grows plain and carved away; when achievements advance, the person's trace retreats.
translations.idiomatic: When name grows loud and ornate, substance thins and is pared away; when merit advances, the man himself recedes.

sentences.zh: 如此則精靈遂越，驕侈自親。

translations.literal: If so, the spirit hastens away and arrogance and extravagance draw near of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then the spirit slips away, and pride and excess draw close unbidden.

sentences.zh: 情與道絕，事與勢鄰。

translations.literal: Feeling and the Way are severed; affairs and power are neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: The heart severs itself from the Way; office and ambition become neighbors.

sentences.zh: 方欲役思以持勢，乘勢以求津。

translations.literal: Just then one would deploy thought to hold power, ride power to seek a ford.
translations.idiomatic: At once one sets the mind to clutch power, and rides power in search of passage.

sentences.zh: 故利欲誘其性，禍難嬰其身。

translations.literal: Thus profit and desire entice one's nature; calamity and hardship attach to one's person.
translations.idiomatic: Profit and craving twist the nature; disaster and peril seize the body.

sentences.zh: 利欲交則幽顯以之變，禍難構則智術無所陳。

translations.literal: When profit and desire intersect, hidden and manifest change thereby; when calamity and hardship take form, wisdom and art have nowhere to display.
translations.idiomatic: Where profit and craving meet, what is hidden and what is plain are altered together; when disaster takes shape, wit and skill have no field in which to act.

sentences.zh: 若然者，雖縻爵帝局，焉得而寧之？

translations.literal: If such a one, though fettered with noble rank at the imperial court, how could he find peace in it?
translations.idiomatic: For such a man, even bound in high noble rank at the emperor's court, what peace can there be?

sentences.zh: 雖結珮皇庭，焉得而榮之？

translations.literal: Though bound with jade pendants in the royal court, how could he find glory in it?
translations.idiomatic: Even jade pendants at the royal threshold--what glory can they bring him?

sentences.zh: 故身道未究，而崇邪之徑已形。

translations.literal: Thus before the Way of the self is exhausted, the path of revering depravity already takes shape.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Way within is fully pursued, the crooked path already shows itself.

sentences.zh: 成功未立，而修正之術已生。

translations.literal: Before success is established, the art of correcting oneself already arises.
translations.idiomatic: Before success is won, the need to repair oneself has already appeared.

sentences.zh: 福祿交蹇於人事，屯難頓萃于時情。

translations.literal: Fortune and salary together stumble in human affairs; hardship and difficulty suddenly gather in the temper of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and office trip together through human affairs; distress suddenly masses in the mood of the age.

sentences.zh: 忠介剖心于白日，耿節沉骨於幽靈。

translations.literal: Loyal integrity lays bare the heart in the bright sun; steadfast integrity sinks bones in the spirit realm.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men lay open their hearts in the light of day; the steadfast sink their bones into the unseen world.

sentences.zh: 因斯愚智之所機，倚伏之所系，全亡之所依，其在遜順而已哉。

translations.literal: Through this--the pivot of foolishness and wisdom, the tie of dependence and decline, the reliance of preservation and destruction--it lies in humility and compliance, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the hinge on which fool and sage turn, the bond that links fortune and fall, the ground on which survival and ruin rest--all of it comes down to yielding and compliance, and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼鑒之！

translations.literal: Alas, take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Take this to heart--mark it well!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼鑒之！

translations.literal: Alas, take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Take this to heart--mark it well!

sentences.zh: 景所著述數百篇見行於世。

translations.literal: Several hundred pieces that Jing composed are in circulation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred pieces written by Jing circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 刪正晉司空張華《博物志》及撰《儒林》、《列女傳》各數十篇云。

translations.literal: He revised and corrected Jin Minister of Works Zhang Hua's Records of Broad Learning, and also compiled several tens of chapters each of Record of the Confucian Forest and Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: He edited and corrected Jin Minister of Works Zhang Hua's Records of Broad Learning, and also compiled several dozen chapters each of Record of the Confucian Grove and Biographies of Exemplary Women, and the like.

sentences.zh: 長子昶，少學識，有文才，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chang, with learning and knowledge from youth and literary talent, died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chang was learned from youth and possessed literary talent, but died young.

sentences.zh: 昶弟彪之，永安中，司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Biao Zhi, during Yong'an, was acting staff officer to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Biao Zhi, during Yong'an, served as acting staff officer to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人云：才未半古，功已過之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The ancients said, 'Talent not half that of antiquity, yet achievement already surpassing it.'
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The ancients said, 'His talent was not half that of the men of old, yet his achievement already surpassed theirs.'

sentences.zh: 王肅流寓之士，見知一面，榮任赫然，寄同舊列，雖器業自致，抑亦逢時之所致焉。

translations.literal: Wang Su was a man adrift from his homeland; recognized in a single meeting, his honored appointments blazed forth, and he was ranked with the former generation--though his capacity and achievements were self-attained, yet it was also what meeting the times brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was a man cast adrift from his homeland; known after one audience, he blazed into lofty office and was treated like the veterans of an earlier age. Though his talent and success were his own, they owed something as well to the age that received him.

sentences.zh: 劉芳矯然特立，沈深好古，博通洽識，為世儒宗。

translations.literal: Liu Fang stood lofty and apart, profound and deep, loving antiquity, broadly penetrating in comprehensive knowledge--master of scholars for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang stood upright and alone, steeped in antiquity, deep and grave, with broad and thorough learning--the age's leading scholar.

sentences.zh: 懋才流識學，見重於世，不虛然也。

translations.literal: Mao's talent flowed and his learning was recognized--esteemed in the world, not without reason.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's gifts were abundant and his learning widely admired; that the world honored him was no empty praise.

sentences.zh: 常爽以儒素著稱，景以文義見宗，美乎。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang was famed for plain Confucian integrity; Jing was honored for literary principle--how fine.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang was celebrated for scholarly simplicity; Jing was revered for the force of his writing--worthy indeed.
